title: A message is written only inside the caller's transaction
statement: A message MUST be written only inside the caller's transaction, after its payload is checked. When the service declares a live event source, a notice MUST follow the commit and never precede it; when it declares none, Enqueue MUST send no notice, so a transaction with effects takes no notify lock at commit.

title: One worker holds one message under a lease
statement: A message MUST be claimed by at most one worker at a time under a lease, only the current lease MUST be able to finish it, and a late result MUST NOT count as a success.

title: Delivery is in order per key
statement: Messages MUST be delivered in order within one key, where a key is the tenant, the destination and the resource key together, so the same resource key of two tenants is two keys; the order index, the lock hash of the key, every predicate per key and the blocked view MUST include the tenant; a retry MUST block only its own key and MUST keep the message identity, and an unknown destination MUST stay queued.

title: A database failure is never a delivery
statement: A database failure MUST NOT be counted as a delivery, a lost claim result MUST keep the lease, a failed claim MUST return nothing, and a process crash MUST leave every rule intact.

title: The worker and its subscriptions are bounded
statement: Worker concurrency and subscriptions MUST be bounded by checked limits, a lost session MUST stop every subscription, and shutdown MUST finish a completed delivery and return a cancellation as such.

title: The queue keeps no error text, and the blocked view lists each stuck key once
statement: The queue MUST store no error text or payload copy, and the blocked view MUST list each stuck key once.

title: The delay from commit to delivery is measured per destination
statement: The worker MUST record, for each message that reaches done, the time from its enqueue in the caller's transaction to done as the histogram outbox.delivery.delay in seconds labelled by destination only, and MUST report the age of the oldest message of each destination that is not done as the gauge outbox.oldest.age, so the time a committed change takes to reach its destination is known and can be alerted on.

title: A message moves only through the dispatch states
statement: A message MUST be in exactly one of the states pending, dispatching, outcome unknown, reconciling, done, parked and discarded, and MUST move only by these transitions: pending to dispatching by a claim; dispatching to done, to pending, also when the handler returns a conflict (ST-SUP-RP01-LC18), to outcome unknown or to parked; outcome unknown to dispatching, to reconciling or to parked; reconciling to done, to pending, to parked or to reconciling again; and parked to done, to pending or to discarded by a person; any other transition MUST be refused and MUST leave the message as it was.

title: An outcome is unknown when the request may have reached the destination
statement: An error that the handler marks as a conflict MUST end in pending as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 states, also when the attempt's deadline has passed. Otherwise, an attempt MUST end in outcome unknown when its deadline passes, when the connection is lost after the request was sent, when the handler returns an error that it does not mark as not sent, as refused by the destination or as a conflict, or when its lease expires while it is dispatching; only a success MUST end in done, an error marked as not sent or as a transient refusal MUST end in pending, an error marked as a conflict MUST end in pending as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 states, and an error marked as a permanent refusal MUST end in parked.

title: An unknown outcome is sent again only to an idempotent destination, with the same key
statement: From outcome unknown, a message MUST be dispatched again only when its destination is registered as idempotent, and every attempt MUST send the same outgoing idempotency key, which the message stores at enqueue as the key that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06), or as its message identity when no inbound key exists; a message for a destination that is not registered as idempotent MUST NOT be dispatched again from outcome unknown.

title: Reconciling asks the destination's status lookup
statement: From outcome unknown, a message for a destination that is not idempotent and registers a status lookup MUST move to reconciling, and the worker MUST call the lookup with the message identity and its outgoing key only after the attempt's deadline plus the destination's settle time has passed; a lookup that answers acted MUST move the message to done, one that answers not acted MUST move it to pending, and an answer of unknown or an error MUST keep it in reconciling with a backoff until the lookup bound, a worker setting whose default is 10 lookups, moves it to parked.

title: A message with no safe next step is parked with an alert
statement: A message MUST move to parked when its outcome is unknown and its destination is neither idempotent nor has a status lookup, when its lookups are exhausted, when its handler marks a permanent refusal, or when its attempts are exhausted and its destination is not registered as must land (ST-SUP-RP01-LC23); parking MUST record the state the message left, MUST raise one alert event and metric that name the destination and that state, MUST hold back the later messages of its key and MUST NOT hold back another key.

title: A person resolves a parked message
statement: Resolve MUST accept only a parked message, with an allow for the resolve permission (ST-SUP-RP01-LC17), the principal of the person who resolves it (ST-SUP-RP01-LC17) and the outcome they chose: acted, not acted, or discarded; for a destination registered as idempotent it MUST accept only not acted, or discarded when the destination must land, because sending it again is safe and acted would lose what the delivery records; acted MUST move the message to done, not acted to pending with the same identity and outgoing key, and discarded to discarded, which releases its key; discarded MUST be refused for a destination that need not land; the resolution MUST write its audit row in the same transaction as the state change; and a resolution without an allow, or of a message in any other state, MUST be refused and change nothing.

title: A destination is registered with its idempotency and its status lookup
statement: A destination MUST be registered on the worker with its name, its handler, whether it is idempotent, whether its messages must land, and an optional status lookup with its settle time; a destination that does not say it is idempotent or must land MUST count as neither; a status lookup without a positive settle time MUST be refused; and a destination that is neither idempotent nor has a status lookup MUST be accepted, and its unknown outcomes MUST be parked.

title: An unknown outcome is claimed under a lease and holds back its key
statement: A claim MUST move a dispatching message whose lease has expired to outcome unknown in the same statement, before it claims anything for that key; a message in outcome unknown or reconciling MUST be claimed under a lease as a pending one is, when its backoff time has come, by the worker that then takes its next step; and a message in dispatching, outcome unknown or reconciling MUST hold back the later messages of its key, so a refund never overtakes a charge whose outcome is unknown.

title: Purge removes only parked messages that may go
statement: Listing dead letters MUST return only parked messages, and purge MUST remove only parked messages, in bounded batches, and MUST NOT remove one that left outcome unknown or reconciling, or one of a destination registered as must land, until a person resolves it; purge MUST NOT remove a discarded message.

title: Resolve decides the resolve permission itself
statement: Resolve MUST itself ask the decision port the worker is built with whether the person's subject has the permission resolve on the resource outbox_destination:<destination name>, for the destination that the request names, qualified with the tenant of the caller's transaction, which under the tenant policy is the tenant of the parked message, in the form of ST-SUP-RP06-LC22, at the consistency floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, and MUST refuse a deny or a port error; a worker built without a decision port MUST refuse every resolution; and Resolve MUST NOT take a decision from its caller. Resolve MUST take the subject only from a principal that the authorization runtime makes, never from a string of its caller, and MUST decide before it reads the message, so a refusal of the permission gives one answer for every message, one that is not there, one of another tenant or destination, and one in any state; only after an allow MAY it answer that the message is not found or not parked. The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), from finding 4 of the security baseline review of the runtime. So a resolve grant serves one tenant, and tenant provisioning (ST-DECL-UC10) MUST write the operator's resolve grant for each tenant it provisions. The orchestrator decided this change under the owner's delegation (2026-11-09); review of PR #157.

title: A consumer conflict is dispatched again with backoff and is not an attempt
statement: When a handler returns an error marked as a conflict, such as RunConsumer does (ST-SUP-RP10-LC26), the dispatch MUST move the message from dispatching to pending (ST-SUP-RP01-LC08), MUST NOT count an attempt, MUST count one conflict in a counter of the message, MUST make the message due again after a wait that starts at 100 ms, doubles at each conflict in a row up to 30 s and has random jitter, and MUST hold back the later messages of its key while it waits, as for a retry. A dispatch that does not end in a conflict MUST set the counter to zero. After 20 conflicts in a row, the dispatch MUST count each further conflict as a failed attempt, so a message that does not stop conflicting still ends as the attempts limit states (ST-SUP-RP01-LC12).

title: The queue is tenant-owned, and only the relay functions span tenants
statement: The queue table stego_outbox.messages MUST have row-level security enabled and forced, with the tenant policy on the transaction-local tenant setting, USING and WITH CHECK, for the runtime role (ST-STD-TXN-R01); Enqueue, Resolve and the listing of dead letters MUST run under that policy in a transaction of one tenant (ST-SUP-RP04-LC03), so a tenant can neither see, write nor resolve a message of another tenant. The operations that span tenants MUST run only through SECURITY DEFINER functions of the schema stego_outbox: the claim, the lease-checked move and release of a claimed message, the purge, the blocked view and the oldest age. Each such function MUST be owned by the NOLOGIN role stego_outbox_relay, MUST set search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, MUST use schema-qualified names only, and MUST restore any setting it changes. The role stego_outbox_relay MUST have its own policy on the queue table for SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE and none for INSERT, and it MUST be the only policy on the queue table apart from the tenant policy (ST-STD-TXN-R01). EXECUTE on these functions MUST go only to a separate worker role, which the worker mode connects as; the request-path runtime role MUST NOT get it, MUST hold only SELECT and INSERT on the queue table under the tenant policy, and MUST hold no UPDATE or DELETE, so it cannot set a message's state itself. Resolve MUST change a message's state only through a relay function that requires the message's tenant_id to equal the transaction-local tenant. Every relay function MUST check its arguments in SQL and refuse any other value: a claim limit of at most 32; a lease from 1 second to 5 minutes; a bounded delay and due time; an attempts change of -1, 0 or 1; nothing returned on a lease token that does not match; and a release only from outcome_unknown or reconciling. The purge of parked messages MUST refuse a negative age and MUST never remove a must-land message, which a must_land column records at enqueue. The move MUST require the message's tenant_id to equal the transaction-local tenant when that setting is set. The migration MUST revoke CREATE on the schema from stego_outbox_relay in the same transaction that creates the functions, and MUST document the role membership it needs to create objects owned by that role (SET and INHERIT). The claim MUST return each claimed message with its tenant, and every later step of that message, its handler and its audit row, MUST run in a transaction of the message's tenant (ST-STD-TXN-R04). The runtime role MAY call stego_outbox.resolve without the permission check that Resolve makes in Go, because that permission is an authorization decision at the provider and cannot be made in SQL. This risk is accepted: the function changes only a parked row of the caller's tenant, under the rules of ST-SUP-RP01-LC13, so the worst case is that a revocation is marked failed or a message is sent again, and no completion can be forged. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08).

title: The listener session comes from the connector package
statement: The live event source MUST take its LISTEN session through the Listener interface of the outbox package, and the runtime library MUST provide the one adapter of that interface in its connector package pgconn (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06), so no service writes its own; the adapter MUST open its session from a direct DSN or the connection configuration of the PostgreSQL adapter's opener, and MUST refuse at start a DSN that names a transaction-mode pooler. Before it connects, the adapter MUST make the checks of tenant.Open: the pooler guard (ST-SUP-RP04-LC04) and the transport check (ST-SUP-RP04-LC09), so it refuses a session setting and a DSN or configuration whose TLS does not verify the server, such as sslmode disable, allow, prefer or require, unless the loopback test mode is set and every target is a loopback IP address; so no startup message and no password go to a server that is not verified. On the session it MUST run the pooler guard's check of app.tenant. The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), from finding 2 of the security baseline review of the runtime.

title: A live event is a hint for one tenant
statement: Subscribe MUST take a tenant.Tenant and MUST refuse the zero tenant. A notice MUST carry only the message identity, with no tenant ID, no destination and no resource key, because any role with CONNECT on the database can LISTEN on the channel and read every notice. For each notice the source MUST read the message again by its identity under row-level security in a transaction of each subscriber's tenant, MUST deliver the event only to a subscriber whose read finds the row, and MUST drop it for every other subscriber, so the filtering per tenant happens at that read; a notice that cannot be read MUST be counted and skipped and MUST NOT stop the source or a subscription. An event MUST be a hint only, and the subscriber MUST act only on what the read under row-level security returns.

title: Each dispatch counts as an attempt at the claim
statement: The claim MUST count one attempt for each message it moves to dispatching, in the claim's own statement, so a crash after the send keeps the count; the count MUST be taken back only for what is not an attempt: the first 20 conflicts in a row (ST-SUP-RP01-LC18), an unknown destination, and a worker that stops before it sends; a success MUST take nothing back, and the count MUST never fall below the attempts made.

title: The attempts limit is bounded, and a must-land message is never parked for a retry
statement: The worker's attempts limit MUST default to 25 and MUST be refused outside 1 to 1000; a message of a destination registered as must land MUST NOT be parked when its attempt ends as not sent or as a transient refusal, whatever its attempt count, and MUST stay pending with its backoff, so a provider that is down holds back its key and raises the oldest-age alert (ST-SUP-RP06-LC14) instead of waiting for a person.

title: Done messages are purged after a bounded retention
statement: The worker MUST purge done messages whose done time is older than the configured retention, on a timer, in bounded batches through the relay's purge function (ST-SUP-RP01-LC19); the retention MUST default to 7 days and MUST be refused below 1 hour; no other runtime contract MAY read a done message after its retention, so a purge never changes what another package answers (ST-SUP-RP06-LC18).

title: A destination can follow its messages' state in the same transaction
statement: A destination MAY register a state hook, which the worker MUST call in the transaction of each state change of a message of that destination to done, parked, pending from parked, or discarded, with the message identity, its group identity given at enqueue and the new state, so a package can keep its own record of a group of messages that a purge does not remove; a hook that returns an error MUST roll back the state change.

title: Stopping the claims does not cancel a handler in flight
statement: StopClaiming MUST end only the claiming of new messages; each handler in flight MUST keep a work context that ends only when the worker's parent context ends or when the drain bound of the context given to Finish ends, so a handler that honours its context finishes during a rolling deploy; Finish MUST wait for the handlers in flight until that bound, and MUST NOT report finished before a Run that has started stops claiming.

title: A handler panic is an unknown outcome
statement: The dispatch MUST recover a panic of a handler, MUST move the message to outcome unknown with the code handler-panic and no panic value stored, and MUST keep the worker running, so a panicking handler is never sent the message again blindly (ST-STD-TXN-R14).

title: A destination sets its payload limit up to 1 MiB
statement: The queue MUST take a payload limit per destination, from 1 byte to 1 MiB, and refuse a payload above its destination's limit, or above 64 KiB for a destination that sets none, before it reads or writes the database. The queue table MUST store the payload as bytea, exactly the bytes that Enqueue checked as one JSON object, with a check of their length up to 1 MiB; a migration MUST change an earlier jsonb column to bytea, and change the check only when its definition differs, adding it NOT VALID and then validating it, each step with a lock timeout. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde. The migration from a jsonb column MUST refuse to run, with an error that says to drain them first, while any audit-sink message is open, since jsonb kept its values but not its bytes. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); final check of PR #178 at 437d9c18.

title: The worker gives the oldest age of one destination
statement: The worker MUST give Worker.OldestAge(ctx, destination), the age of the oldest message of the destination that is not done, or zero when it has none, read through the same relay function as the gauge outbox.oldest.age (ST-SUP-RP01-LC07), so a caller such as the relay's watch (ST-SUP-RP06-LC14) reads it without a metric pipeline; a read that fails MUST give an error, never zero. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator, who decided it on 2026-11-10 in the review of PR #181 (ST-SUP-Q69). Until the runtime change lands, the generated watch reads the gauge.

title: Every item reaches its action unchanged, one key at a time
statement: A queued item MUST reach its action with its content unchanged and never merged with another, equal keys MUST run serially while other keys continue, and a change that arrives during a key's action MUST request a later pass.

title: The queue is bounded with backpressure
statement: Worker count, key capacity and reconnect delay MUST be refused outside their bounds, and each producer MUST hold at most one key waiting for admission.

title: Retries are off by default, bounded, and retry only the action
statement: The zero retry policy MUST make one attempt, a policy MUST be refused beyond four attempts or outside one millisecond to one second of delay, each attempt MUST get a fresh budget, cancellation MUST stop a delay, and a scan, window, checkpoint or denied error MUST NOT be retried.

title: A reconnect keeps the schedule
statement: Across watch sessions the queue MUST keep its keys, their order, due times, capacity and a failed scan's capped backoff, and an interrupted action MUST run again.

title: Scans resume after the last success with opaque cursors
statement: A scan MUST resume from the cursor of the last item whose action succeeded, MUST treat cursors as opaque and refuse an oversized or non-UTF-8 one before any read, and MUST return incomplete progress without error at its page budget.

title: A stream is bounded and closed
statement: A stream MUST have separate open and receive limits, MUST stop with the scan contract error past its item limit, MUST be cancelled and joined when the scan returns, and a value the receive function returns after its receive timeout MUST NOT reach the emitter.

title: Each operation is its own trace with a fixed outcome, and telemetry holds no private value
statement: Each reconciliation, scan and sweep MUST start its own trace root, MUST end with exactly one of success, failure, timeout or cancelled, and no metric, snapshot or exposition MUST carry a key, payload, error text or resource ID.

title: Overlapping controllers share one private provider set, and a failed callback emits one event
statement: Overlapping controllers in one process MUST share one private telemetry provider set that the first starts and the last closes, the monitor MUST bind loopback only, and a callback failure MUST emit exactly one service.failed event with no formatted cause.

title: A retry never outruns its budget
statement: A retry delay MUST be refused when it exceeds the action timeout; a failed attempt MUST be cancelled and its callback joined before the delay starts; no further attempt MUST start when the remaining work budget cannot cover the delay and a full action; a terminal peer failure MUST cancel the pending retries of a parallel cycle; and a later success MUST NOT clear a failure already stored in the cycle checkpoint.

title: Backoff follows its cause
statement: A failed connection attempt MUST NOT delay keys already queued, an interrupted action MUST take the next capped delay rather than a reset one, a successful scan MUST clear the scan backoff, and a queued action MUST be able to run while the next scan waits for its due time.

title: Admission never blocks a producer
statement: The scan cursor MUST advance only after the item is admitted, the page request context MUST end before the scan waits for admission, admission MUST stop on cancellation, and adding a key MUST NOT block the caller.

title: One collector per controller, fixed in size
statement: A collector that another running controller holds MUST be refused; the collector MUST expose a fixed instrument set, the running gauge stego_controller_running, queue capacity, queued, active, retrying, waiting and ready, completed actions by outcome, retries, completed scans, reconnects, one fixed duration histogram, and the gauge stego_controller_cleanup_enabled with the cleanup gauges when a cleanup source is set, with no configurable label and a size that does not grow with the resource count; counters MUST survive a reconnect.

title: The monitor serves metrics on loopback only, within fixed limits
statement: The monitor MUST serve the metrics, and nothing else, in Prometheus text format with no-store and nosniff, answer not found to any other path and method not allowed to any other method, register on no default mux, bind loopback only, and run with header, read, write and idle limits and the http.Server MaxHeaderBytes setting of 4096, which Go enforces with its own margin of 4096 bytes; an empty address MUST give a nil collector and no server; a listener failure MUST stop the controller from starting; and when either part exits the monitor MUST close the listener, cancel the shared context and join both.

title: Startup shares one telemetry runtime
statement: The monitor MUST start the telemetry runtime before the application callback and hold it for the callback's whole life, so that setup, nested controllers and deferred cleanup share one runtime and one instance identity; it MUST wait for an ongoing bounded provider close; each queue MUST register once, unregister when its run ends, and be refused beyond sixty-four; cancellation MUST emit no failure event; the callback's value and error identity MUST return unchanged; and a probe command MUST start no telemetry.

title: Each operation logs once, at a severity its outcome sets
statement: Each reconcile, scan and watch MUST emit one completion log and one duration sample that carry the operation, the outcome, the retry flag and the span's trace and span IDs, valid also when unsampled; a watch span MUST cover one session and end before reconnect; the log MUST be INFO for success and cancellation, WARN for a failure that retries and ERROR for one that does not; watch start, reconnect and cleanup-summary failure MUST be fixed events; and the instruments MUST be the fixed stego.controller.* set with no configurable label.

title: A sweep validates first and classifies each failure
statement: A sweep MUST validate every definition before it starts telemetry and MUST start no provider when its context is already cancelled; it MUST register no keyed queue; a pass deadline MUST count as a retry only while the run is active and the error is not terminal; a page callback that returns no error after its deadline MUST be recorded as a timeout and MUST NOT become a source error for the terminal policy; and the sweep MUST join its workers before the next page and before close.

title: Scan progress is exact
statement: On a source or emitter error a resumed scan MUST return the progress of the completed prefix together with the error; it MUST refuse a page above its size bound and bound each page read by the operation timeout; a scan from the beginning MUST return the scan contract error, not partial progress, when its page budget cannot cover the source; and a scan MUST start no background work.

title: Cleanup sampling is its own bounded worker
statement: With metrics enabled the runtime MUST read the cleanup summary on its own worker, under the action timeout and at the resync interval, join it on shutdown, and never read it when metrics are disabled; a failed read MUST keep the last values but mark them unavailable, shutdown MUST mark them unavailable, a malformed sample or a terminal access error MUST stop the controller, any other failure MUST be reported and sampled again, and a failed sample MUST keep its own counter and never count as a work retry.

title: An operation root keeps its context and bounds its span
statement: An operation root MUST keep the supplied context's cancellation, deadline and runtime ownership and change trace ancestry only; a database span MUST be a child of the current operation; sampling MUST apply to each operation root; a controller span or log MUST carry no resource key, provider response, credential or private error text; and attribute and link counts per span MUST stay within the default limits.

title: Controller logs reach standard error when no collector is set
statement: When the telemetry runtime has no collector endpoint, each controller completion log and each failure log MUST also be written to standard error as one JSON line with the same fields and the same rules for private values as ST-SUP-RP02-LC15 states, so a controller without a collector still has its logs.

title: Without a collector, no provider
statement: When no collector endpoint is set the runtime MUST start no provider and open no connection, and the service MUST serve as if telemetry were absent, except the built-in console events of ST-SUP-RP12-LC22.

title: Export is bounded, verified and never retried
statement: Export MUST go over one verified HTTPS gRPC connection owned by private providers with no global, each export MUST finish inside its deadline, send at most one MiB and never be retried, and startup MUST NOT wait for the collector.

title: Queues drop rather than block, and failures are counted safely
statement: The trace and log queues MUST be bounded and drop rather than block the request, and each failed export batch MUST be counted per signal and answered with a fixed safe error.

title: One span per request or call, named by the pattern, never the URL
statement: The runtime MUST start one server span per HTTP request and one RPC span covering the whole call, named by the method and the registered route or protobuf method when bounded and _OTHER otherwise, and never by the URL.

title: A failure marks the span without a message
statement: A status of 500 or more, a panic or a failing RPC status MUST mark the span with a fixed error type and MUST NOT attach a message, a cause or a value.

title: Every call is measured and logged once, sampled or not, with no private data
statement: Request duration metrics and one completion log per call MUST exist whether or not the span is sampled, MUST be correlated with the span when it is, and MUST hold no raw path, resource ID, body, credential or user detail.

title: The server span starts before authentication and ends with the transport status
statement: The HTTP and RPC server span MUST start before authentication and capacity admission and end only after the final status is known, MUST NOT change authentication, capacity reservation, stream identity expiry, I/O deadlines or shutdown of the observed call, and the public health and discovery routes MUST stay outside the request span, metric and log wrappers.

title: A valid parent continues the trace, and the remote flag never decides sampling
statement: A single valid traceparent MUST continue its trace ID and parent ID, and the remote sampled flag MUST NOT change the local ratio decision at any ratio.

title: Settings have fixed defaults and a fixed shape
statement: With a collector endpoint and no exporter setting, traces, metrics and request logs MUST be enabled; the sampling ratio MUST default to 0.1, the metric export interval to ten seconds and the service name to the declared service name; the protocol setting MUST be absent or grpc; and the certificate setting MUST be read only as a bounded regular PEM file, with the system roots when it is absent.

title: Export limits are fixed numbers
statement: The trace queue MUST hold at most 256 spans, exported in batches of at most 32; each export MUST end within two seconds with a 64 KiB response limit; and shutdown MUST give the provider at most three seconds.

title: Request metrics have fixed names, units and labels
statement: The runtime MUST emit http.server.request.duration and rpc.server.call.duration as histograms in seconds with fixed boundaries through 1,800 seconds and cumulative temporality, labelled by method, registered route or RPC method, status and a fixed error class; MUST emit http.server.active_requests and rpc.server.active_requests as label-free up-down counters; and MUST NOT use a trace or span ID as a metric label.

title: A completion log has a fixed name and a severity its outcome sets
statement: The completion log MUST be named http.server.request.completed or rpc.server.call.completed, MUST carry the span's fields, the duration, the trace and span IDs and, for a denied or failed call, the fixed error code that the handler gives, and never the error text, and MUST be INFO for a normal completion, WARN for a denied or failed client request and ERROR for a server failure. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the completion log holds the fixed error code.

title: The RPC span records a fixed attribute set
statement: The RPC server span MUST record exactly rpc.system.name, rpc.method and rpc.response.status_code with one of the seventeen gRPC status names; only UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE and DATA_LOSS MUST mark it failed, with error.type equal to that status name; and no server span MUST carry a resource ID, a user identity, a peer address or error text.

title: The route pattern survives a copied request and zero sampling
statement: The span, metric and log MUST carry the registered route pattern also when authentication copies the request and when the sampling ratio is zero, and metrics and logs MUST NOT take their fields from recorded span attributes.

title: A runtime package starts an operation span through the runtime
statement: The runtime MUST offer an operation span that another runtime package starts: the caller MUST choose root or child explicitly, the span name MUST come from a closed set registered when the runtime starts, the attribute keys MUST be fixed, at most 8, and a finish function MUST set the outcome and an error status with no message. SpanEvent MUST accept such a span, and the runtime MUST export it with its own record only, as ST-SUP-RP03-LC05 states for its own spans. The probe runtime MUST use it to start a child span per call.

title: A Tenant is never zero and comes only from its three sources, which the code holds by type
statement: A Tenant MUST be built only inside the package and only from one of three sources: a verified identity claim, through an Identity value that only the authentication runtime can make; a tenant column read from a row through the package's own row reader, which serves the tenant list of the iterator (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07) and the claimed outbox row of the outbox worker, which the staging transaction wrote from its own tenant (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16); and the tenant that a Provision or Retire request names, through a Decision value that only the authorization runtime can make after the permission is decided (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09). The data of an Identity and of a Decision MUST live in a mark of the module's internal seal package: seal.IdentityMark holds the tenant claim and whether it is present, and seal.DecisionMark holds the allowed tenant ID and the action it was decided for, provision or retire; only a constructor of the internal package can make a mark that is not zero. The package MUST read that data only through seal.TenantOf and seal.DecisionOf, which call an unexported method of the mark that returns the mark's own data, and MUST NEVER read a method that an outer type can declare again, such as TenantClaim or Allowed; a zero mark, a nil embedded interface, or a value whose mark is not one the internal constructor made MUST give no tenant. Requested MUST take the action it serves and MUST give a tenant only when both the Decision's tenant ID and its action are the ones requested, so a Decision serves only the one action on the one tenant. The package MUST NOT export a function, field or conversion that builds a Tenant from a string. Every function that takes a Tenant MUST refuse the zero value before any statement is sent, and a client-supplied header or body field and a message payload MUST NOT be accepted as a source.

title: The context carries one tenant or fails
statement: Reading the tenant from the request context MUST return the tenant the authentication component set there, and MUST return an error and never a zero tenant when none is set, so no code path reachable from a request runs without a tenant.

title: Every transaction starts with a transaction-local tenant setting and ends with it unchanged
statement: The transaction helper MUST run SELECT set_config('app.tenant', $1, true), or the same call schema-qualified as pg_catalog.set_config, as the first statement of every transaction it opens, before the caller's first statement, and MUST NOT run a session-scoped SET or set_config with is_local false. Before it commits, the helper MUST check that current_setting('app.tenant') still equals the transaction's tenant, and MUST roll back with an error when it does not. When a connection comes back to the pool with app.tenant set outside a transaction, the helper MUST close that connection and not give it out again. Each error of the commit helper that ends before COMMIT is sent MUST be marked as not committed (ErrNotCommitted), so a caller can tell it from a COMMIT whose outcome is not known. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: The pooler guard refuses a session setting
statement: The guard MUST refuse at startup a connection option, a startup parameter or a statement that sets a session-scoped value, and MUST verify on the first connection that current_setting('app.tenant', true) is empty outside a transaction, so a pooled connection never carries one tenant to the next client.

title: A multi-tenant worker opens one transaction per tenant
statement: Each MUST iterate the tenants it is given and open one transaction per tenant with that tenant set, MUST NOT share a transaction between two tenants, and MUST continue with the next tenant after one tenant's function fails and report every failure at the end.

title: The owner connector serves only the migration job
statement: The owner-role connector MUST open only when the process runs the migration job and MUST refuse to open in the api, worker or controller mode, and the runtime connector MUST verify at startup that its role owns no table and is not a superuser and holds no BYPASSRLS, neither directly nor through a role that it is a member of, and fail startup otherwise.

title: The tenant list is the tenants table that provisioning writes
statement: The iterator MUST read the tenants that it visits from the table stego_tenants of the service's database, in tenant ID order, as the runtime role, and MUST skip each tenant that has a retire time; only Provision and Retire of the tenant runtime, which the generated service serves as its own commands (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09), MUST write that table, through SECURITY DEFINER functions of the owner role that set search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp and name every object with its schema; Retire MUST set the retire time and delete no row, and each MUST run the provisioning hooks that the generated code registers in the same transaction as its write, with that tenant set, so a hook's writes commit with the tenant or not at all. stego_tenants MUST have a CHECK on its ID that refuses the same IDs as the package's own ID check: from 1 to 255 bytes, and no character of the Unicode general categories Cc, Cf, Zl or Zp. The migration text of the tenant runtime that makes stego_tenants and its two functions MUST run again with no error on a database that it made, and the migration job of the service runtime MUST run it in its tables step (ST-SUP-RP14-LC03). The orchestrator decided ST-SUP-Q97 (a) on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation: the table, its CHECK and its functions are the same for every service (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05), so Provision and Retire can follow with no schema change.

title: A runtime can tell a pool that tenant.Open returned
statement: Opened(db) MUST report true only for a pool that Open or OpenOwner returned and that is not closed, and false for any other pool, a copy of a pool value and a closed pool; it MUST keep no pool alive, and a reused address MUST NOT match. The command and query runtimes MUST refuse in their constructors a pool for which Opened reports false (ST-SUP-RP10-LC30, ST-SUP-RP11-LC14). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: tenant.Open takes the connection configuration of the adapter's opener
statement: tenant.Config MUST take a connection configuration that the PostgreSQL adapter's opener builds, and Open and OpenOwner MUST open the pool with that configuration as it is, so that the verified TLS policy of ST-SUP-RC01-OC01 to OC04 and the pool bounds of ST-SUP-RC01-OC12 hold on the pool that the command and query runtimes take; Guard MUST check that configuration as it checks a DSN (ST-SUP-RP04-LC04). Decision of 2026-11-09, which the Product owner delegated to the orchestrator, from the question of the PostgreSQL adapter builder on ST-SUP-RC01-OC41. Open and OpenOwner MUST refuse a connection string whose TLS does not verify the server, such as sslmode disable, prefer, require or allow, as they refuse such a configuration; only Config.InsecureLoopback, the loopback test mode of the adapter's opener, lets a configuration or a connection string connect without verified TLS, and only to a loopback IP address, as the adapter's test mode does: a name such as localhost and a socket path are refused. Decision of 2026-11-10 by the orchestrator, under the Product owner's delegation, in the second review of PR #187. Decision of 2026-11-10 by the orchestrator, under the Product owner's delegation, in the review of PR #187.

title: An audit event has a fixed shape, and its request fields are untrusted
statement: Event MUST carry exactly id (UUID v7), occurred_at, recorded_at, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_kind (user, service, system or impersonated_by), actor_ip, user_agent, action, operation, on_behalf_of, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (ok, denied or failed), error_code, request_id, trace_id, span_id, idempotency_key, before, after, patch, service, service_version, declaration_version, hash_version, prev_hash and hash; operation is the name of the declared command, query or worker that wrote the row, or empty for a row of the runtime itself; on_behalf_of is the staging principal on whose behalf a consuming worker acted (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16), or empty; actor_ip and user_agent MUST be marked untrusted and MUST NOT decide anything. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: The audit row commits with the change, or alone with its outcome
statement: Recording an audit entry MUST insert the row through the caller's transaction and MUST NOT commit on its own, recording an outcome MUST write the row of a denied or failed mutation in its own short transaction with the outcome and error_code, and a read of an entity that holds a pii field MUST be recorded in its own short transaction with the action read, so the read row stays when the caller's transaction rolls back.

title: Redaction before storage: pii is redacted, secret is never stored
statement: The encoder MUST replace every field declared pii in before, after and patch, at any depth of a nested value, with the fixed redaction marker before hashing and storing, also when the service's Audit setting declares audit.pii keep (ST-DECL-EN10), which keeps the field in the source record only, and MUST drop every field declared secret, at any depth, before it encodes a value, so it reaches neither the row, the hash, the sink nor an error message.

title: The hash is SHA-256 over the canonical redacted record and prev_hash, in one chain per tenant
statement: The canonical encoding MUST be deterministic, with sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace and one form for numbers and times; hash MUST be SHA-256 over the canonical redacted record followed by prev_hash; each tenant of each service MUST have its own chain (ST-STD-TXN-R01), in which each row has a seq one higher than the row before it; prev_hash MUST be the hash of the previous row of the same chain, and the first row's prev_hash MUST be 32 zero bytes. The canonical encoding MUST include operation and hash_version, and hash_version MUST be 2 for every row that carries operation; the canonical encoding of hash_version 3 MUST also include on_behalf_of, and every new row MUST have hash_version 3; a verifier MUST read hash_version 1 rows, which have no operation, and hash_version 2 rows, which have no on_behalf_of, each with its own encoding. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: The patch is RFC 6902 over the redacted states
statement: Diff MUST produce an RFC 6902 patch from the redacted before to the redacted after, applying that patch to before MUST yield after exactly, and a metadata-level event MUST carry neither before, after nor patch.

title: The verifier walks one tenant's chain from its checkpoint and checks it against every anchor
statement: Verify MUST walk one tenant's chain in seq order in a transaction of that tenant (ST-SUP-RP04-LC03), from the row after the chain's latest retention checkpoint (ST-SUP-RP05-LC11) with the checkpoint's hash as the first prev_hash, or from the first row with 32 zero bytes when the chain has no checkpoint. It MUST check each retention checkpoint against the retention anchors that the sink holds for the chain, and MUST report as forged a checkpoint that has no retention anchor of the same seq at the sink or whose hash differs from it, and then walk from the latest checkpoint that the sink confirms. It MUST recompute every hash and report the first row whose prev_hash or hash differs, and MUST report a first row whose seq is not one higher than the checkpoint's seq. For each periodic anchor that the sink holds for the chain, it MUST compare the hash of the row whose seq equals the anchor's count with the anchor's head, MUST report truncation when the highest seq is lower than the latest anchor's count, and MUST report as forged an anchor whose count is lower than an earlier anchor's count or whose head is not on the chain. It MUST check each row as it reads it and keep only the previous hash and the anchors, so its memory does not grow with the chain.

title: Every audit row is enqueued for the sink, keyed by its id
statement: Record MUST enqueue the same event in the outbox for the audit sink in the same transaction, with the message key equal to the event id, and the destination MUST deliver it through the Sink port and treat a duplicate id as success, so the sink is idempotent. The sink message MUST carry operation and hash_version with the other fields. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: The sink is a port with no way back
statement: The Sink port MUST expose only Append(events) and Anchor(anchor), where an anchor holds the tenant, the kind periodic or retention, the head hash and the count; the runtime MUST NOT expose an update, a delete or a read on it, and the service MUST reach the sink only through the outbox destination, never directly from a handler.

title: The anchor job anchors each tenant's chain at fixed boundaries under the fenced lease
statement: The anchor job MUST, for each tenant through the per-tenant iterator (ST-SUP-RP04-LC05), publish a periodic anchor with the hash of the chain's row with the highest seq and that seq as the count, read from the audit table and never from the chain-head row, to the sink through the outbox, with the tenant on the outbox row (ST-SUP-RP04-LC01). It MUST run only under the controller lease and MUST fence each anchor transaction with the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03), as ST-SUP-RP10-LC20 states for a worker run. Its period boundaries MUST be fixed clock times, the multiples of the anchor period since the Unix epoch. It MUST store the last anchored boundary of each chain in audit_anchor_boundaries in the anchor's transaction, and a holder MUST publish at once a boundary that is due and not anchored, also just after it takes the lease. When more than one boundary is due, it MUST publish one anchor for the latest, MUST count the earlier due boundaries that get no anchor of their own as skipped, and MUST count the anchored boundary as late when it is published after the next boundary is due. A boundary that is due and not anchored MUST be a health signal until it is anchored.

title: The audit tables are partitioned, tenant-walled and append-only, and one owner function maintains them
statement: The DDL text MUST create the audit table partitioned by month on recorded_at, with no default partition; a trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the table and on each partition; the tables audit_chain_heads, audit_anchor_boundaries and audit_retention_checkpoints; row-level security enabled and forced on each of the four tables, with one policy on the transaction-local tenant setting (ST-STD-TXN-R01); and for the runtime role SELECT and INSERT only on the audit table, SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE only on audit_chain_heads and audit_anchor_boundaries, and SELECT only on audit_retention_checkpoints (ST-STD-TXN-R06). It MUST create the function audit_maintain(), owned by the owner role, SECURITY DEFINER, with a fixed search_path and no arguments, whose retention is the audit-log setting at the time the migration runs, with EXECUTE granted to the runtime role only. Each call MUST set a lock timeout, by default 2 s, and MUST do at most one step in the caller's short transaction: create the first missing partition of the current month and the next three months, or write the retention checkpoints of the oldest partition older than the retention (ST-SUP-RP05-LC11) and drop that partition whole; it MUST return whether a step is left, and MUST NOT delete rows. The controller MUST call it in a loop under the controller lease, each call in its own transaction fenced with the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03), and a missing partition for the next month MUST be a health signal. The owner connector stays for the migration job only (ST-SUP-RP04-LC06). The text MUST run again with no error on a database that it made, in one transaction: a table or an index is made only when it is missing, a function or a trigger is replaced, and a policy is dropped before it is made again, so the migration job runs on every release. Decision of 2026-11-10 by the orchestrator, under the Product owner's delegation, in the review of PR #187.

title: A partition drop leaves a retention checkpoint of each chain
statement: Before it drops a partition, the maintenance function (ST-SUP-RP05-LC10) MUST, in the same transaction and for each tenant whose chain has rows in that partition, set the transaction-local tenant to that tenant, write one row into audit_retention_checkpoints with the seq and the hash of the chain's last row in the partition, and enqueue the same values to the sink as an anchor of the kind retention with the tenant on the outbox row. audit_retention_checkpoints MUST have a trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, so a checkpoint cannot be moved after it is written.

title: Record writes a transaction's events as one batch and takes the chain lock last
statement: Record MUST take all the audit events of one transaction in one call, MUST lock the chain head of the transaction's tenant once, as the last lock that the caller takes before it commits, and MUST give the events consecutive seq values in the order given. It MUST set recorded_at of each event after it holds the lock, to the greater of the database clock and the chain's last recorded_at, and MUST ignore a recorded_at that the caller gives, so recorded_at never falls along a chain and a partition drop never cuts a chain in its middle. RecordOutcome and RecordRead MUST each lock the head of their tenant's chain in their own short transaction. Because the command runtime calls Record only after the fill returns (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06), a read row that the fill causes never waits on the chain lock of its own command; one chain per tenant with this late lock is enough, and a read row needs no chain of its own. A RecordRead of a request whose Record rolled back MUST NOT fail as a read after the record: the command runtime clears the mark of an attempt that did not commit (Writer.Forget), because that attempt holds no chain lock any more. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: Untrusted values are cleaned, states pass the redaction, and no value reaches an error
statement: New MUST clean each untrusted value, actor_ip, user_agent, request_id and idempotency_key, before it is hashed and stored: it MUST replace invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD, remove NUL and cut the value to at most 512 bytes of valid UTF-8. before, after and patch MUST be settable only through the redacting path of ST-SUP-RP05-LC03, never as raw values. An error that the package returns MUST NOT carry a field value. RecordOutcome and RecordRead MUST always give the event a new ID. A failed RecordOutcome MUST be counted, and returned as an error that names no value, so the command runtime can log its metadata (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06).

title: The audit runtime gives the outbox adapter and the sink destination
statement: The audit runtime MUST give the adapter that enqueues each audit row for the audit-sink port on the outbox queue of the outbox runtime (ST-SUP-RP01) in the row's transaction, and the outbox destination of the audit sink, in the same form as authz.Relay, so no generated service writes either; the destination MUST be registered as idempotent and must land. The audit-sink destination MUST carry a payload of up to 1 MiB, and Record MUST refuse an event whose sink message is larger with a fixed error before its first statement, so a command fails clearly and never half-way. This answers the audit builder's question on the writer's outbox enqueuer. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); the payload limit comes from the review of PR #178. The destination MUST deliver the exact bytes that Record enqueued, which must be the canonical sink message, and MUST NOT rewrite them into a canonical form. The exact bytes come from the re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde.

title: The decision port has the AuthZEN shape, and deny is a decision
statement: The decision port MUST offer an evaluation of one subject, action, resource, context and consistency that returns a decision with allowed, token and reason; a batch evaluation of several requests with execute_all as the default semantic; and a resource search by subject, action, resource type, context, consistency and page, with an opaque page token. A deny MUST be a decision with allowed false and MUST NOT be an error.

title: The relationships port writes idempotently and returns the written-at token
statement: Relationships MUST expose Touch(tuples, preconditions) and Delete(filters, preconditions), both idempotent on retry and both returning the token the provider wrote at, and the port MUST be reachable only by the relay destination, never by a handler or a slot fill.

title: The floor is at_least(token), and minimize-latency does not exist
statement: Consistency MUST be either fresh or at least as fresh as a token, the runtime MUST NOT expose a minimize-latency or an exact-snapshot option, and an evaluation MUST refuse a zero consistency, so every check runs at least as fresh as the token stored on the resource row.

title: A token is opaque, is stored per row, and is never compared
statement: The authorization token MUST be an opaque value with a text column form stored on every protected row, and STEGO MUST NOT parse, order or compare two tokens, because the revision of some SpiceDB datastores, such as the PostgreSQL datastore, is a snapshot with only a partial order; only the provider may judge how fresh a token is. A read of one row MUST check at least as fresh as the service's revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), and at least as fresh as the row's token only while the floor is zero. A list that pages the database and filters each page by batch evaluation MUST check each page at least as fresh as the floor read at the time of that page, so no later page is checked against an older state than the newest delivered revocation. The pages are not one snapshot, because ST-SUP-RP06-LC03 forbids an exact snapshot: a relation written while the list is paged MAY change what a later page shows.

title: The SpiceDB provider maps the port one to one
statement: The SpiceDB provider MUST speak gRPC, map fresh to fully_consistent and at-least-as-fresh to at_least_as_fresh, write with TOUCH and DELETE only, and MUST NOT expose at_exact_snapshot. For a resource search of more than one page, the opaque page token MUST hold the after_result_cursor together with the consistency of the first page, and every later page MUST send that consistency again unchanged, because SpiceDB binds the consistency into the cursor; each later page's results MUST then be filtered with one CheckBulkPermissions call at least as fresh as the floor read at the time of that page, and only the allowed results returned, so a later page is in force at the current floor although its cursor keeps the first page's consistency.

title: The relay is FIFO per resource key and parks a poison entry
statement: The outbox destination authz MUST be registered as idempotent and as must land, MUST deliver tuples in order per resource key, MUST store the returned token on the owning row, and MUST park an entry that fails with a permanent error, raise an alert and continue with the other keys, so one malformed write never halts the relay and a parked entry leaves only when it is sent again.

title: Every principal is a subject, and a service account is one too
statement: Subject MUST map the Identity to the declared subject type and an id built from both the token's issuer and its subject, so two verifiers with the same subject value never map to one subject; a worker, controller or relay MUST call with its own service_account:<name> subject, and the package MUST expose no bypass flag, setting or subject.

title: Caveat context is a map, and a missing field is an error
statement: Context MUST be a string-keyed map built from the declared context fields, and a CONDITIONAL_PERMISSION result or a missing caveat field MUST be returned as an error, not as a deny, because it means the declaration forgot a context field.

title: The handle decides at the floor and declares relations only through the outbox
statement: The handle MUST be bound to the current transaction and tenant. Its evaluation MUST call the decision port with the transaction's principal as subject and, as consistency, at least as fresh as the service's revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13); only while the floor is zero, at least as fresh as the row token, and fresh when the row has no token either. The handle MUST read the floor through its own bound transaction and never through a second connection of the pool, so a request never waits for a second connection while it holds one. Its relate and unrelate MUST enqueue a touch or delete tuple in the transaction's outbox for the authz destination and MUST NOT call the provider.

title: The handle holds only its allowed relations and no provider
statement: Handle MUST be constructed with the allowed relation set the generated code passes it, MUST refuse any other relation with an error before enqueueing anything, MUST give a system principal its service_account subject, and MUST expose no provider client, no relationships port and no bypass.

title: Every provider passes the conformance suite
statement: The conformance suite MUST run one allow and one deny per permission and the new-enemy test, in which a check at least as fresh as the token of a removed relation denies; search MUST be an optional group, and a provider that does not search MUST report so, after which every list uses batch evaluation.

title: A transaction's tuple writes are one revocation, complete only when the relay lands it
statement: A transaction MUST have one revocation, with its identity known before the commit, which every tuple the transaction enqueues joins, touch or delete, from Relate, Unrelate or a relationship mapper, through any handle bound to that transaction, because a touch can also remove access (view = viewer - banned). The revocation's identity MUST be kept in a transaction-local setting, which the first tuple write of any handle sets and every later write reads, so two Binds on one transaction share one revocation. Relate and Unrelate MUST return that one revocation; Wait MUST be Status (ST-SUP-RP06-LC15) that waits until the state is no longer pending or its context ends, and MUST be refused before the commit; and a revocation is complete only when the relay lands every tuple of it.

title: After a revocation lands, every check of the service is at least as fresh as its token
statement: The relay MUST keep the service's revocation floor in the table authz_floor: one row that holds one token, with at most a local sequence number for diagnostics that MUST NOT be used to order tokens. To write a tuple, touch or delete, the relay MUST raise the floor in one short transaction of its own: it locks the floor row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, then sends the tuple and a TOUCH of one fixed marker relationship to the provider in one WriteRelationships request, then writes that request's written_at token to the floor row and commits, and stores the same token on the owning row. A head read MUST NOT be used, because the provider can share one head revision between callers and return a revision from before the relay's own write. Because the one write commits after the lock is granted, its token is at least as fresh as the tuple and as every earlier floor, on every datastore and with any overlap strategy, so the floor never falls and no two tokens are compared. The lock MUST be held for that one provider call only. So authz deliveries serialize on the floor lock, and the throughput is one provider write at a time for each service; this is accepted because the relay is the FIFO must-land destination (ST-SUP-RP06-LC06). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08). Every single evaluation, batch evaluation and resource search, and every page of a list, MUST run at least as fresh as the floor, so a write that removes access through a group, an exclusion or a subject in two tenants is in force on every resource of every tenant once its delivery is done. The floor and the checks MUST work on every SpiceDB datastore, the PostgreSQL datastore included.

title: A revocation that is not delivered in time raises an alert
statement: The relay MUST raise one alert event and metric that name the destination authz on each upward crossing of outbox.oldest.age{destination=authz} (ST-SUP-RP01-LC07) past the delivery alert bound, and none while the gauge stays above the bound. A read of the gauge that fails MUST be counted and MUST raise the same alert, and MUST NEVER be skipped without a signal, so a broken gauge cannot hide a late revocation.

title: A revocation status is read only by the tenant and principal that made the write
statement: Status MUST read a revocation by its identity from its record (ST-SUP-RP06-LC18) only for the tenant and principal that made the write and MUST answer not found to any other pair; and it MUST report failed when a person discarded any tuple of the revocation, otherwise parked while any tuple is parked, otherwise pending until every tuple is done, complete with the service's revocation floor as it is read in the transaction in which the last tuple becomes done when all are done, and expired after the record's retention. Because that floor is raised before each tuple is done (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), it is at least as fresh as every tuple of the revocation, and no two tokens are compared.

title: The delivery alert bound defaults to 5 seconds and is positive
statement: The delivery alert bound MUST default to 5 seconds when no bound is given, and the relay MUST refuse a bound that is not positive.

title: The Decision that the tenant runtime takes comes only from this package
statement: The value that tenant.Requested takes (ST-SUP-RP04-LC01) MUST be made only by this package: DecideTenant MUST take the tenant ID that the Provision or Retire request names and the action, provision or retire, decide that action's permission at the floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09), and, only on an allow, build the value's seal.DecisionMark through the constructor of the module's internal seal package with exactly that tenant ID and that action, so an allow serves only the one action on the one tenant and no package outside the runtime module can make one; a deny MUST give no such value.

title: A revocation's status is kept in its own record
statement: The authorization runtime MUST keep one row for each revocation in the tenant-owned table authz_revocations, with its identity, the tenant and principal that made the write, its tuple count, its counts of done, parked and discarded tuples, and, once every tuple is done, the floor token that ST-SUP-RP06-LC15 reports; the row MUST be written in the transaction that enqueues its tuples and MUST be changed only through the outbox state hook (ST-SUP-RP01-LC25) in the transaction of each tuple's state change, through the function of ST-SUP-RP06-LC21; when the hook makes the last tuple done, that function MUST store the floor as it reads it in that transaction, which the relay raised before the tuple became done (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13); and Status MUST read only this row, never the outbox, so the purge of done messages (ST-SUP-RP01-LC24) never changes its answer. The row MUST be kept for a configured retention of at least 30 days, after which Status MUST answer expired.

title: The staging principal of a consumed message comes from a sealed constructor
statement: The package MUST offer one constructor of a Principal from the principal column of a claimed outbox row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16). It MUST take a value of the type staging.Staging, which only staging.NewStaging makes; the type and its constructor MUST live together in the internal package internal/staging of the runtime library, because Go lets only the package that declares a type with an unexported field make a value of it. Only the command runtime (ST-SUP-RP10) MAY call staging.NewStaging, from RunConsumer only, and only the command runtime and this package, which only names the type, MAY import internal/staging. A test of the module MUST refuse any other importer, any other caller and a dot or blank import of the package; this guarantee is held by that test, not by the compiler. So only the command runtime's RunConsumer can build a staging principal, and a consumer decides as it (ST-SUP-RP10-LC17) with no bypass. The Principal MUST map to the same subject as the identity that made the staging write, and the constructor MUST refuse an empty or malformed principal and the subject *.

title: A provider error carries fixed text and no subject or caveat value
statement: Every error that the package returns or logs MUST carry a fixed text for its provider status code and kind, and MUST NOT carry the provider's message, a subject ID, a caveat value or a context value, in its text or in any error it wraps; a tuple MUST be named in an error, a park record, a log or telemetry by its resource type, resource ID and relation only. Whether the error is refused, transient or a context error MUST stay readable by kind.

title: The migration keeps the runtime role out of the floor, the revocation counts and the outbox states
statement: Migration MUST refuse a runtime role that equals the relay login role or is a member of it, and a relay login role that equals a hook (worker) role. The SECURITY DEFINER functions MUST be owned by a NOLOGIN role apart from the relay login role, and the relay login role MUST hold UPDATE on authz_floor only (ST-SUP-RC29-OC06). On the revocation record table authz_revocations (ST-SUP-RP06-LC18), the runtime role MUST hold SELECT, and INSERT only on the columns of the revocation's identity, tenant, principal and tuple count, never on a count of done, parked or discarded tuples or on the token, and no UPDATE or DELETE. The counts and the token MUST be changed only through one SECURITY DEFINER function, authz_revocation_state, with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp and schema-qualified names, which the outbox state hook (ST-SUP-RP01-LC25) calls. The function MUST change a count only when the outbox message it names has the destination authz and is in the new state the hook reports, MUST refuse the state done unless session_user is a hook role, and MUST refuse to run under an isolation other than READ COMMITTED. So the runtime role cannot lower the floor, set an outbox message to done, or mark a revocation complete. The text MUST run again with no error on a database that it made, in one transaction: a table or an index is made only when it is missing, a function or a trigger is replaced, and a policy is dropped before it is made again, so the migration job runs on every release. Decision of 2026-11-10 by the orchestrator, under the Product owner's delegation, in the review of PR #187.

title: A resource ID at the provider names its tenant
statement: Because a key is unique only within its tenant (PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, id)), every resource ID that STEGO sends to the provider MUST be the tenant-qualified form: the unpadded base64url form of the tenant ID, a /, and the unpadded base64url form of the row key, which is injective and within SpiceDB's ID characters. The separator MUST be /, because a person's subject ID holds a | (ST-SUP-RP06-LC07), so a resource ID and a person's subject ID never have the same shape and are never equal, also when a tenant ID equals an issuer; a service account name MUST NOT hold a /. This form MUST be used in every tuple the relay writes, as resource, as a subject set and as a direct subject of a resource type, such as the folder of an arrow parent, in every evaluation and batch evaluation, and in every resource search; the handle and the relay MUST refuse a tuple whose resource, subject set or direct subject in the resource shape is of another tenant. A search result MUST be mapped back to a row only when its tenant part equals the transaction's tenant and its type is the type searched, and MUST be dropped and counted otherwise. So a principal allowed on a key of one tenant is never allowed on the same key of another tenant. One exception: the floor marker relationship (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13) is of the whole service, holds no tenant data, grants no permission and is never checked, so its IDs stay unqualified. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154. The orchestrator decided this change under the owner's delegation (2026-11-09); review of PR #157.

title: The key table is scoped by tenant, principal and key
statement: The migration text MUST create idempotency_keys with tenant_id, principal_id, key (at most 255 characters), fingerprint, status (in_progress or completed), response_code, response_headers, response_body, locked_at and expires_at, with the primary key (tenant_id, principal_id, key), so one client's key never collides with another's.

title: The key row is inserted first and completed in the same transaction
statement: Wrap MUST insert the key row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING inside the store's write transaction before the handler runs, and MUST write status completed, the response code, headers and body and expires_at in that same transaction, so a crash leaves no key without its row and no row without its key.

title: A duplicate in progress gets 409, a changed body 422, and a match a replay
statement: When the insert returns nothing, Wrap MUST SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT the row and answer 409 idempotency-key-in-progress when the lock fails or status is in_progress, 422 idempotency-key-reused when the fingerprints differ, and otherwise replay the stored code, headers and body byte for byte with Idempotent-Replayed: true without running the handler.

title: A transient failure stores nothing
statement: A response with status 5xx, 429 or 503, and a 409 with the code conflict (ST-SUP-RC32-OC10), MUST NOT be stored and its key row MUST go with the rollback, and an operation declared as requiring the key MUST answer 400 when the Idempotency-Key header is absent or is not a structured string.

title: The fingerprint is SHA-256 over method, path and canonical body
statement: Fingerprint MUST be the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 over the method, the path and the canonical JSON body, each part prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, where canonical JSON has sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace and one form for numbers, so the same request gives the same fingerprint on every replica. A body with an object that repeats a key, or holds two keys that are equal under case folding, MUST be refused, since a decoder may act on either value. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde.

title: An outgoing key derives from the inbound key with its scope, the destination and the effect
statement: Derive MUST return the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 over the tenant ID, the principal ID, the inbound key, the destination name and the effect name, which the declaration gives each outgoing call, each part prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer. Derive MUST return the same value on every retry of the same inbound request, so a fan-out from one inbound request is idempotent at every destination. Two tenants or two principals that send the same inbound key MUST NOT get one outgoing key, and two effects of one request at one destination MUST NOT get one outgoing key, because the inbound key is unique only in the scope of ST-SUP-RP07-LC01.

title: Purge is a bounded batched delete at 24 hours
statement: Purge MUST delete rows whose expires_at has passed in batches of a bounded size with a pause between batches, MUST NOT delete row by row or rely on a TTL index, and the default retention MUST be 24 hours.

title: The conformance tests cover replay, reuse, race and crash
statement: The conformance suite MUST prove a replay of the same body, 422 for a different body, 409 for a concurrent duplicate, and that a crash before commit leaves no key row, and every store that binds the wrapper MUST pass it.

title: A purge job runs Purge on a declared interval
statement: The runtime MUST offer a purge job that runs Purge on the interval the service declares, one minute by default, stops when its context ends, never runs two purges at once, and reports a failed run without stopping, so a generated service only builds the job and registers it (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09). The first purge MUST run at start, each wait MUST end with the context, and a purge that the context ended MUST NOT count as a run. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde.

title: A fingerprint over a declared field list
statement: The runtime MUST offer a fingerprint over a declared list of body fields: it MUST decode the JSON body, keep only the named fields, and return Fingerprint over the method, the path without its query and the canonical form of that kept body (ST-SUP-RP07-LC05), so a generated service emits only the field list of each operation (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09). It MUST refuse a body whose keys repeat or are equal under case folding anywhere in it, as Fingerprint does. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde.

title: The key table is tenant-owned, and only the purge function spans tenants
statement: The key table idempotency_keys MUST have row-level security enabled and forced, with the tenant policy on the transaction-local tenant setting app.tenant, USING and WITH CHECK (ST-STD-TXN-R01), so a request can neither see, write nor delete a key row of another tenant. The purge across tenants MUST run only through the SECURITY DEFINER function idempotency_keys_purge(timestamptz, integer) in the schema of the key table, which MUST be owned by the NOLOGIN role stego_outbox_relay, MUST set search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, MUST name the key table with its schema, MUST take no cut-off later than the clock of the database, so a caller cannot remove a key whose retention has not ended, and MUST refuse a limit outside 1 to 10000. The role stego_outbox_relay MUST have a policy on the key table for SELECT and DELETE, and one for UPDATE whose WITH CHECK is false, so it can lock the rows it deletes and change none, and none for INSERT. PUBLIC MUST NOT get EXECUTE on the function; the runtime role MUST get EXECUTE on it from the grants of the migration job, and MUST NOT get DELETE on the key table. The migration text MUST run again with no error on a database that it made, also as an owner role that is not a superuser and holds membership in stego_outbox_relay WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT TRUE. The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), from finding 1 of the security baseline review of the runtime.

title: Money is int64 minor units with a currency, and adds only within one currency
statement: Money MUST hold an int64 amount of minor units and an ISO 4217 code, Add and Sub MUST return an error when the currencies differ, MUST return an error on overflow, and the package MUST expose no float conversion.

title: Allocation loses no minor unit
statement: Allocate MUST split an amount by the given ratios into parts whose sum equals the amount exactly, assign the remainder one minor unit at a time in a fixed order, and MUST refuse an empty or all-zero ratio set.

title: A transfer is written by one owner function call that must balance and keep the limit
statement: Post MUST write the transfer and at least two entries through one call of the owner function ledger_post, which inserts them in one statement. The function MUST refuse the set when the debits do not equal the credits, when an entry names no account of the ledger, or when an entry's currency differs from the ledger's. It MUST lock FOR UPDATE, in account ID order, only the accounts declared with a balance limit, and MUST refuse the transfer when it takes such an account below its limit, with open pending debits counted, as ST-STD-TXN-R17 states for a sum limit. The runtime role MUST NOT be able to insert a transfer or an entry in any other way.

title: A pending transfer is immutable, and it is posted or voided once
statement: Pend MUST write a pending transfer through the owner function ledger_pend, and no later call MUST edit its amount or entries. Posting or voiding it MUST write a new row that names it, through ledger_post_pending or ledger_void. The function MUST refuse a post whose entries are not a split, per side, of the pending transfer's entries on the same accounts, and MUST refuse to post a pending transfer whose expiry has passed by the database clock. The state machine MUST return already_posted, already_voided, expired or exceeds_pending as its only errors, so a change to a pending transfer is a void and a new pend.

title: A retried transfer returns the original, and a reused key with another body is refused
statement: Each transfer MUST store a fingerprint of its body: the kind, the code, the entries, effective_at, and pending_id or reverses with the amount. Post, Pend, PostPending, Void and Reverse MUST insert with ON CONFLICT (ledger_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING.
