A retry with a key already used and the same fingerprint MUST return the original transfer and insert no entry; a retry with the same key and another fingerprint MUST return ErrKeyReused and write nothing. Transfer IDs MUST be compared in lower case, so a retry that names the ID in upper case is the same call.

title: A reversal is a new transfer that names the original, at most once
statement: Reverse MUST insert, through the owner function ledger_reverse, a new transfer whose entries are exactly the original's entries with each side swapped, MUST set reverses on the new row and reversed_by on the original, MUST refuse a transfer that is already reversed or not posted, and the package MUST expose no difference adjustment.

title: A balance derives from entries after the latest snapshot, on the account's normal side
statement: Balance MUST return the latest snapshot plus the sum of the entries posted after it, signed by the account's normal balance (debit or credit), the balance at a time MUST select by effective_at, and every entry MUST keep both effective_at and posted_at. A snapshot MUST be computed inside the owner function ledger_snapshot, with through_xid = pg_snapshot_xmin(pg_current_snapshot()); no caller supplies its amount. A pending hold whose expiry has passed MUST NOT count against a balance limit. An effective_at in the future MUST be refused, and an effective_at before the ledger's declared close date MUST be refused.

title: The snapshot and check jobs run under the lease, and a failed check is a health signal
statement: Snapshot MUST write one balance_snapshots row per account after the declared number of entries. Check MUST verify that every ledger sums to zero and that each snapshot equals the snapshot before it plus the entries between them, never by a sum from the first entry, and MUST report a pending transfer that is not voided more than one sweep period after its expiry as a failure of the expiry sweep (ST-SUP-RP08-LC11). Both MUST run in controller mode under the lease with the fencing token, each transaction MUST end before the lease deadline and set a lock_timeout, and a failed check MUST mark the service unhealthy. Check MAY keep its last checked position in memory only; after a restart it MUST read the ledger once again from the first snapshot. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08).

title: The ledger tables are written only by owner functions, and the guards refuse every change
statement: The DDL text MUST give the runtime role SELECT only on accounts, transfers, entries and balance_snapshots, and EXECUTE on the owner SECURITY DEFINER functions ledger_open, ledger_post, ledger_pend, ledger_post_pending, ledger_void, ledger_reverse and ledger_snapshot, and on the read functions that run as the caller. Each function MUST set search_path to pg_catalog, pg_temp, use schema-qualified names, check that its tenant is app.tenant, and check every argument. The DDL text MUST hold the declared account codes of each ledger, each with its normal side, hot flag and min_balance, and ledger_open MUST take only the account ID and the code and refuse an account ID that exists with a typed error. A BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger MUST raise on transfers, entries and accounts; the transfer status MAY change only through the post and void functions and only from pending. balance_snapshots MUST have no foreign key to accounts.

title: A ledger call refuses an isolation that can overdraw
statement: Every ledger call that writes MUST refuse a transaction whose isolation is not READ COMMITTED, before any write, because under REPEATABLE READ a balance read after the row lock can see an older state and overdraw a limited account, and a SERIALIZABLE writer beside a READ COMMITTED writer can overdraw it as well.

title: An expiry sweep voids each expired hold
statement: A controller sweep MUST void each pending transfer whose expiry has passed, through Void with the derived idempotency key expire:<transfer ID>, in a transaction of its tenant under the lease with the fencing token, so a hold that a client abandons never reserves funds for ever.

title: Each currency has its minor-unit exponent, and test and metal codes are refused
statement: Money MUST refuse the codes XTS, XAU, XAG, XPT and XPD, and MUST give for each accepted ISO 4217 code its minor-unit exponent from ISO 4217, such as 0 for JPY, 2 for USD and 3 for BHD.

title: A mode is a named component set, selected by a repeatable flag with all as the default
statement: Parsing the modes MUST accept the mode option more than once and the STEGO_MODE environment value, which holds a comma-separated list of modes, MUST use the mode options alone and ignore STEGO_MODE when any mode option is given, MUST default to all, MUST refuse an unknown mode at startup, and the registry MUST map each mode name to a component set the generated code registers, never to a fixed bundle.

title: A lease is one row; Acquire and Renew are two UPDATEs that increment the token
statement: Acquire MUST run UPDATE leases SET holder=$1, expires_at=now()+ttl, token=token+1 WHERE name=$2 AND (holder=$1 OR expires_at<now()) RETURNING token. Renew MUST run its own statement, UPDATE leases SET expires_at=now()+ttl, token=token+1 WHERE name=$2 AND holder=$1 AND token=$3 AND expires_at>=now() RETURNING token, where $3 is the token that the holder holds, and MUST NOT run the statement of Acquire, so a renew after the lease expired, was taken over or was released takes nothing and leaves the row as it is. The defaults are lease 15 s, renew 10 s and retry 2 s, and the package MUST NOT use a session-scoped advisory lock.

title: Every write under the lease carries the fencing token and fails on a higher one
statement: A write made through the lease MUST carry the holder's token, MUST fail with the fenced error when the lease row holds a higher token, and the holder's loop MUST stop on the fenced error.

title: A holder that cannot renew stops before the lease expires
statement: When Renew fails or returns a different token, the holder MUST stop its work within one renew interval and before expires_at, and MUST NOT act on the lease after that time.

title: Each mode has its own readiness
statement: Ready MUST answer per mode: api ready when the HTTP server accepts requests, worker ready when the database is reachable, controller ready when the database is reachable, whether or not it holds the lease, its controller queue is running and ready, and no backfill of it is stalled (ST-SUP-RP09-LC12), and a replica MUST report not ready as the first step of shutdown.

title: Each mode shuts down in its own order
statement: On SIGTERM the sequencer MUST, for api, fail readiness, wait the endpoint propagation delay and drain in-flight requests; for worker, stop claiming and finish the claimed rows; for controller, flush the checkpoint under the lease with the holder's token and then release the lease; and the sequencer MUST run the sequences of every selected mode.

title: The checkpoint row carries the fencing token and refuses a lower one
statement: The checkpoint statement MUST update the change's row in stego_schema.backfills only when the row's token is not higher than the holder's, MUST set the row's token to the holder's, and MUST fail with the fenced error when the row holds a higher token, so that the row lock orders two writers and a stale holder cannot move the checkpoint after a newer one.

title: Backfill progress goes through the probe as counts
statement: The backfill MUST report each batch, the rows that fail the conversion, the duplicate groups, completion and a stall only as the built-in schema backfill observations of the probe runtime (ST-SUP-RP12-LC23), with counts and the change ID and no row value.

title: A backfill batch is one short transaction
statement: Each backfill batch that the generated controller runs MUST be one transaction with a lock timeout, by default 2 s, over at most the batch size, by default 1,000 rows, after the checkpoint key in key order, and MUST write the checkpoint in that transaction. The checkpoint MUST store the key with its type, one of integer, uuid, text and composite, and MUST compare keys in the order of that type, never as the text of another type. A composite key MUST be stored as the ordered list of its parts, each with its type and its value prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, and compared part by part as a row comparison; a text part compares in the collation of its column, as the batch's ORDER BY does.

title: The backfill resumes from its checkpoint and marks completion
statement: After a restart or a takeover the backfill MUST start after the checkpoint key, and when a batch finds no row left it MUST mark the change complete with its time.

title: A new fill value starts a repair pass
statement: When the declared fill value of a retype differs from the fill digest in its checkpoint row, the backfill MUST clear the completed time and the checkpoint key, record the new digest, and pass again over the rows whose new value is unset.

title: A stalled backfill fails readiness, never liveness
statement: A backfill with rows left that commits no batch for three lease TTLs MUST make the readiness of the controller mode (ST-SUP-RP09-LC05) not ready and emit schema.backfill.stalled, MUST NOT fail liveness or stop the process, and MUST make readiness ready again when its next batch commits.

title: A periodic job runs in controller mode at its declared interval
statement: The modes runtime MUST give a periodic job component that runs a registered job in controller mode under the lease, at the job's declared interval, with the first run at start; a run that fails MUST be counted and reported as a health signal and MUST NOT stop later runs. The audit anchor job runs on it at the declared anchor_period, 1h by default, and the audit maintenance at its own declared interval. This answers the audit builder's question on what calls the anchor job. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: The handle is bound to one transaction, tenant and principal
statement: Handle MUST be constructed only with the open store transaction, the tenant and the principal that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose the tenant and the principal for reading only, with no way to change any of the three. The handle MUST be bound only to a transaction at READ COMMITTED, which binding checks with current_setting('transaction_isolation'), so the revocation floor is read fresh for each statement (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09) whatever the role's default isolation is. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: No raw database connection is reachable through the handle
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose a *sql.DB, *sql.Tx, *sql.Conn, a driver connection or a method that takes SQL text, and MUST reach storage only through the generated, tenant-scoped repository operations of the entities the command declares it writes.

title: Every read and write runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set
statement: Each repository operation the handle offers MUST run in the bound transaction, with the transaction-local tenant set and the tenant predicate added, so a fill cannot read or write a row of another tenant.

title: The handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor
statement: The handle's authorization part MUST be the authorization runtime's handle bound to the same transaction, tenant and principal, so each decision a fill asks for runs with the principal as subject at the consistency floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 states, and MUST offer no other decision path and no bypass.

title: The command's permission covers its declared writes
statement: The command's declared permission, decided before the fill on the command's resource (ST-SUP-RC32-OC06, ST-SUP-RP10-LC31), MUST cover the writes the handle makes to the entities the command declares it writes, and each locked read and each write of a row of an entity with a resource type MUST also decide the command's permission on that row at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, besides the entity's read permission, and answer a deny as not found, so a fill cannot act on a row other than the decided resource without the same permission on it. A create MUST take the loaded value of each row that the new row refers to through a reference to an entity with a resource type, through the entity's generated Parent, a list (EntitySpec.Parent), and a command MUST give each one that is set, and decide on each the permission that the declaration names for that reference (ST-DECL-EN02), such as customer.place_order and product.view; an optional reference that is not set MUST NOT be decided, and the runtime MUST write the relation of each reference when the row is written; Relate and Unrelate MUST take the loaded value of the tuple's resource, refuse a tuple of another resource, and decide the command's permission on it, or the worker's; and an effect MUST be for a row on which the command's permission is decided, or that the handle locked or wrote. A command that declares no permission decides nothing per write and relates nothing. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde. An entity with a Parent and no resource type takes its authorization from its parent: each locked read of it (GetForUpdate, GetForDelete, ListForUpdate), each update and delete of it, and each effect for it MUST take the loaded value of the parent that the row names, tied as a create's parent is, and decide the permission of the command, or of the worker, on that parent; an update that moves the row to another parent MUST take and decide on both parents. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); final check of PR #178 at 437d9c18. An update that moves a row of any entity with a Parent, also one with a resource type of its own, to another parent MUST take the new parent's loaded value, matched as a create's parent is, and decide the permission of the command, or of the worker, on it. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); re-check of PR #178 at 3053fd2f. A move that changes a reference MUST decide the permission that the declaration names for that reference on the new referenced row, as a create does. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that every reference to an entity with a resource type is a relation that the runtime writes, and that a create and a move decide the permission that the declaration names for each reference.

title: Each write through the handle is audited in the transaction, as one batch at the end
statement: Each write the handle makes MUST buffer its audit event, with the command name as the action, the principal as the actor and the diff redacted by field sensitivity, and Run MUST write the buffered events of the attempt with one call of the audit runtime's Record (ST-SUP-RP05-LC12) in the bound transaction after the fill returns and just before COMMIT, so a write and its audit row commit or roll back together and the chain lock is the last lock the command takes. When the audit runtime's RecordOutcome fails, Run MUST log the event's action, resource type, outcome and error code with no field value, and count the failure. Each buffered event MUST carry the command or worker name as operation (ST-SUP-RP05-LC01). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: Effects leave only through the outbox
statement: The handle's effect staging MUST enqueue each declared effect in the bound transaction's outbox for its declared destination, MUST refuse the destinations authz and audit-sink, so a relationship tuple goes only through the authorization handle (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, ST-SUP-RP06-LC10) and an audit row only through the audit runtime, MUST refuse an effect name that the command's CommandSpec does not declare, as CommandSpec takes the declared effect names, MUST register each destination with the must_land and idempotent that it declares (ST-SUP-RC32-OC12), MUST NOT deliver anything before the commit, and MUST expose no broker client, provider client or network client. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the declared effect names and delivery properties bind the fill.

title: A staged effect carries a key scoped to its tenant, principal, destination, effect and entity
statement: Each effect that the handle stages in Run or RunConsumer MUST name the loaded entity value that it is for (ST-SUP-RP10-LC15), and MUST carry the outgoing idempotency key that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06) over the tenant, the principal, an inbound key, the destination and the effect name, where the inbound key is the command's inbound key, or in RunConsumer the message identity (ST-SUP-RP10-LC19), and then the entity's ID, each prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC21 states for a tick; the message stores that key at enqueue, as ST-SUP-RP01-LC10 states. The handle MUST refuse a second effect of one name for one entity in one call, so a redelivery is idempotent at the destination and two effects of one call never share a key.

title: Only the generated code ends the transaction
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose commit, rollback, savepoint or a way to begin a transaction, and Run MUST end the transaction after the fill returns.

title: The handle is invalid once the fill returns
statement: As soon as the fill returns or panics, before Run commits or rolls back, every method of the handle and of its authorization, audit and effect parts MUST return an error and do nothing, so a fill that keeps the handle, or a goroutine it started, cannot use the transaction.

title: Run calls the fill inside the idempotency wrapper
statement: Run MUST call the fill inside the idempotency runtime's wrapper with the same transaction that the handle binds, so the key row commits or rolls back with the fill's writes and a replay of a completed key returns the stored result without calling the fill. A command with an empty key MUST run without the wrapper and leave no key row, so that a PUT, a DELETE and a create or a patch without the header, where the declaration does not require it, need no key of their own; the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: A panic in the fill rolls back everything
statement: When the fill panics, Run MUST roll back the transaction with every write, audit row, outbox row and key row of it, MUST make the handle invalid, and MUST return an error that does not carry the panic value. A fill that does not return normally, also through runtime.Goexit, MUST be treated as a panic: Run MUST return no result, make the handle and its probe invalid and roll the transaction back. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A read through the command handle is authorized and audited as a query read
statement: Each read the command handle makes MUST be authorized as ST-SUP-RP11-LC06 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC07 state for the query handle, and each read of a resource of an entity with a pii field MUST be audited as ST-SUP-RP11-LC08 states, so a command reads nothing that a query of the same principal could not read and leaves the same audit trail.

title: The handle gives the fill its command's or worker's probe
statement: Handle MUST give the fill, through Probe, the typed probe that the generated code built for its command or worker and bound to the handle's span context, tenant, principal and command or worker name (ST-SUP-RC34-OC03), and MUST offer no other probe, writer or logger; as ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 states for the rest of the handle, that probe MUST emit nothing once the fill returns or panics (ST-SUP-RP12-LC02).

title: Each entity value through the command handle is a loaded value
statement: Each read and write operation of the handle MUST return the entity as its generated loaded type, such as LoadedReservation, which carries the stored field values and has no exported constructor, no exported field and no conversion from another type, so a fill can get a loaded value only from the handle and cannot build one itself. Its Value MUST return a deep copy of the stored field values, so a change to a slice or a map that the fill got never changes what the handle later sends, writes or decides on. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A worker handle is bound to its service account and, for a message, to the staging principal
statement: RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST bind the handle to the open store transaction, the tenant of the tick or of the claimed outbox row, and the principal service_account:<worker name> (ST-SUP-RP06-LC07). The effect staging of ST-SUP-RP10-LC07 MUST store with each message for a destination that a worker consumes the staging principal and the name of the staging command or worker, and RunConsumer MUST bind them, for reading only, from the claimed row. None of these MUST come from the fill or from the message payload, and each write's audit row MUST name the worker as the action, the service account as the actor and, in RunConsumer, the staging principal as the principal on whose behalf it acted.

title: A worker handle decides on each resource it touches, and a consumer decides as both principals
statement: Because no request resource is decided before a worker fill, the worker handle MUST decide the worker's declared permission on each resource it reads, as ST-SUP-RP11-LC06 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC07 state for a query, and on each resource it writes, or for a create on the parent resource that the call names, at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 before the write, with the service account as subject. In RunConsumer it MUST make each such decision a second time with the staging principal as subject, built only through the sealed constructor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC19 from the claimed row, and the staging command's or staging worker's own declared permission, which the row's stager names, and MUST allow the read or the write only when both are allowed, so the staging principal is decided on each resource that the payload names and on each other resource that the fill touches, and no principal can make a worker touch a resource that it could not touch through its own command. A deny MUST return the refused error and write nothing, and ST-SUP-RP10-LC05 MUST NOT apply to a worker handle. A worker handle answers a denied read with the refused error, which is also not found, so a worker's fill can tell a deny from a row that does not exist; this is acceptable because the worker's subject is its own service account, its fill is service code and not a client, and the deny is of its own declared permission, so the answer tells no client whether a row exists. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: RunWorker runs one tick of one tenant in one transaction
statement: RunWorker MUST call the fill at most once in one transaction for one tenant and one tick, with no idempotency wrapper, MUST commit only when the fill returns no error, and MUST roll back every write, audit row and staged effect of the transaction otherwise, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC09, ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 and ST-SUP-RP10-LC12 state for Run; each effect that it stages takes the key that ST-SUP-RP10-LC21 gives, not a key of the message identity.

title: RunConsumer calls a worker fill once for each message
statement: RunConsumer MUST insert the consumed message's identity as a key of the idempotency runtime (ST-SUP-RP07-LC01, ST-SUP-RP07-LC02) for the message's tenant and the worker's principal in the bound transaction before it calls the fill, MUST return success without calling the fill when that key is already completed, and MUST use that identity as the inbound key from which ST-SUP-RP10-LC08 derives each staged effect's key, so a message that the outbox delivers again after the commit (ST-SUP-RC18-OC27) changes nothing a second time and stages the same keys.

title: A fenced worker run writes nothing
statement: When the generated code passes RunWorker a held lease, RunWorker MUST lock the lease row with FOR SHARE in the bound transaction right after the tenant setting and before the fill, MUST roll back with the fenced error and not call the fill when the row holds a token other than the holder's, and MUST keep the lock until the transaction ends, so a new holder cannot take the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC02) while the run can still commit, and every write of the run carries the holder's token (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03).

title: A tick's effect has one key on every replica
statement: Each effect that a worker fill stages in RunWorker MUST name the loaded entity value that it is for, and its outgoing key MUST be the one that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06) over the tenant, the worker's service account, an inbound key, the destination and the effect name, where the inbound key is the worker name, the scheduled tick time and the entity's ID, each prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, and the scheduled tick time is the multiple of the interval since the Unix epoch at which the tick is due, as the decimal count of seconds; so every replica that runs the same tick for the same entity stages the same key. The handle MUST refuse a second effect of one name for one entity in one run.

title: A run under a lease ends before the lease can expire
statement: When RunWorker runs under a held lease, it MUST give each tenant's transaction a deadline no later than the lease TTL minus the renew interval after the transaction starts and no later than the lease's expires_at as last renewed, MUST roll back a transaction that reaches the deadline, and MUST NOT commit after expires_at, so the holder stops in time as ST-SUP-RP09-LC04 states; the tenant of a transaction that is rolled back for this reason MUST be run again in the next tick.

title: A locked read holds its row until the transaction ends
statement: Handle MUST offer, for each entity that the command or the worker declares it writes, GetForUpdate and GetForDelete. GetForUpdate MUST lock the row with SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so a concurrent insert of a child row, whose foreign key check takes FOR KEY SHARE on it, does not wait for the lock; GetForDelete MUST lock it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, for a fill that will delete the row or change a column of its primary key, of a unique index or of a key that a foreign key references, so the write does not make the lock stronger later. Each MUST run in the bound transaction, after the tenant setting and with the tenant predicate (ST-SUP-RP10-LC03), MUST first read the row without a lock and decide the read on it, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC13 states for a command handle and as ST-SUP-RP10-LC17 states for a worker handle, which decides as both principals in RunConsumer, MUST NOT lock a row that is denied and MUST return it as not found with no data from it, and MUST decide again when the row's authorization token changed between the read and the lock (ST-SUP-RP06-LC04). The lock MUST stay until Run, RunWorker or RunConsumer ends the transaction, and the handle MUST offer no way to release it earlier. For a rule over a set of rows, such as the last active admin of an organization, the fill of every command, worker or consumer that can break the rule, also one that inserts a row into the set or removes one from it, MUST lock the parent row with GetForUpdate before it writes, and MUST read the set with a statement that starts after it holds that lock, because a row lock does not stop the insert of a new row into the set.

title: A write through the handle carries the version of its loaded value
statement: Each update and delete through the handle MUST take the loaded value that a read or an earlier write of the same transaction returned, MUST write only when the row's resource version is the version that the loaded value carries (ST-SUP-RC01-OC07), and otherwise MUST write nothing, write no audit row and return the conflict error. A write MUST return a loaded value with the new version, so a second write of the same row in the same transaction does not conflict with the first. An update that changes a column of the row's primary key, of a unique index or of a key that a foreign key references MUST take a loaded value that GetForDelete locked, and MUST refuse with an internal error and write nothing when the value was not locked or was locked by GetForUpdate. A write MUST refuse with an internal error, not the conflict error, a loaded value that another transaction returned, such as one that a fill kept from an earlier attempt, and a loaded value of the same transaction whose row a later write through the handle has changed, because a rerun cannot change the result. A delete MUST NOT take a loaded value that GetForUpdate locked, which the delete would make stronger later, and MUST refuse it with an internal error, as for a key change. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: A conflict runs the fill again only as the command declares
statement: Run MUST treat as a conflict the conflict error of ST-SUP-RP10-LC24 and a database error with the SQLSTATE 40001, 40P01 or 55P03 from any statement of the attempt that the fill or the generated code runs, the outbox enqueue and COMMIT included. The statements of the idempotency wrapper are not in this class: a lock that Wrap cannot take with NOWAIT, a lock timeout while its key insert waits on a duplicate key, or a cancel at the deadline during a statement of the wrapper MUST stay the answer 409 idempotency-key-in-progress of ST-SUP-RP07-LC03, with no rerun, and any other database error from a statement of the wrapper, the SQLSTATE 40001 and 40P01 included, MUST be an internal error, with no rerun. Once the handle meets a conflict, every later method of the handle MUST return the conflict error and do nothing, and Run MUST treat the call as a conflict whatever the fill returns, so a fill cannot ignore a conflict and commit. On a conflict Run MUST roll back the whole transaction as ST-SUP-RC32-OC05 states and, while fewer reruns than the command's Retry on conflict (ST-DECL-EN18) have run and the deadline allows a rerun (ST-SUP-RP10-LC28), MUST call the fill again after a random wait of at most 50 ms times the number of the rerun, capped and checked as ST-SUP-RP10-LC28 states, in a new transaction that the generated code opens with the tenant set as ST-SUP-RC32-OC04 states, with a new handle, the same idempotency key (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11) and a new decode of the request body, so a fill that changed its request does not see its change again. Run MUST NOT call the fill again when the outcome of COMMIT is not known, such as when the connection is lost during it or the deadline cancels it (ST-SUP-RP10-LC28), and MUST then return an internal error, for which the handler writes an audit row with the outcome failed and the fixed error_code commit_outcome_unknown in its own short transaction (ST-SUP-RC32-OC07); when that commit took effect, its own audit row with the outcome ok stays as well, so a retry of the client with the same key replays the stored result or runs the command once. After the last attempt Run MUST return the conflict to the handler. Each attempt is one call for the probe (ST-SUP-RP12-LC20): its emissions are held, counted against the limit and sent as their observation counts for that attempt alone.

title: A conflict in a worker run rolls back and waits for the next run
statement: RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST treat a conflict as ST-SUP-RP10-LC25 states and MUST NOT run the fill again in the same transaction or the same tick. RunWorker MUST roll back that tenant's transaction and MUST run that tenant again in the next tick, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC22 states for a deadline. RunConsumer MUST roll back the message's transaction with its key row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC19) and return an error marked as a conflict, not as a failure, so the message is not completed and the relay dispatches it again as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 and ST-SUP-RC18-OC29 state, with the same outgoing keys. In RunConsumer, a deny of the staging principal and a declared refusal of the fill give the same answer on every dispatch, so RunConsumer MUST return them as a permanent refusal, which parks the message, and MUST NOT let them hold back the message's key without end. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: A locked list is bounded and locks only allowed rows in key order
statement: Handle MUST offer ListForUpdate only for an entity that declares it writes and that declares Lock at most (ST-DECL-EN02, ST-DECL-INV81). ListForUpdate MUST first read the matching rows without a lock, with a limit of Lock at most plus one, and when more rows than Lock at most match MUST lock nothing, return no row and return an internal error, never the conflict error and never a shorter list. It MUST then filter the rows by the decision port as ST-SUP-RP10-LC13 states for a command handle and as ST-SUP-RP10-LC17 states for a worker handle, MUST lock only the allowed rows, with SELECT ... WHERE the primary key is one of them, the list's filter applied again and ORDER BY the primary key FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so two fills that lock the same rows lock them in one order, MUST decide again each locked row whose authorization token changed after the first read (ST-SUP-RP06-LC04) and leave out a row that is now denied, and MUST return the locked, allowed rows in primary key order. The locks MUST stay as ST-SUP-RP10-LC23 states.

title: A lock wait ends before the request deadline as a conflict
statement: Before each statement of an attempt that can wait for a row lock, which includes each read with a lock and each write through the handle, the statements of the generated code after the fill and COMMIT, Run, RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST set SET LOCAL lock_timeout in the bound transaction to the smaller of the command's declared Lock timeout (ST-DECL-EN18), or 2 s for a command that declares none and for a worker, and the time left before the deadline of the request or the run less 50 ms, and to at least 1 ms, so a statement that waits for a row lock ends with the SQLSTATE 55P03, which is a conflict (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25), and no lock wait holds a pooled connection without a limit. The first setting MUST come right after the tenant setting and before the idempotency key insert (ST-SUP-RP07-LC02). A cancel at the deadline, or another context error, during a statement before COMMIT MUST also count as a conflict, also when the driver closes the connection on the cancel, as pgx does. During COMMIT, a cancel or another context error MUST count as an outcome of COMMIT that is not known (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) and never as a conflict, because the commit can have taken effect. Run MUST cap the random wait before a rerun (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) so that at least 100 ms is left before the deadline after the wait, MUST check the time left after the wait, and MUST NOT start a rerun when less than 100 ms is left then; it MUST then return the conflict of the attempt before it.

title: Read audit rows have connections of their own
statement: The generated store MUST keep a pool of at least two connections apart from the main pool, which only the short audit transactions of ST-SUP-RP05-LC02 use, so the read audit row of a fill that holds row locks and a main connection never waits for a main connection, and MUST give each such transaction a lock timeout and a statement timeout of at most 2 s, so an audit write that cannot finish fails the read as ST-SUP-RP11-LC08 states and does not wait without a limit.

title: The command runtime commits and opens its pool only through the tenant runtime
statement: Run, RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST open each transaction with tenant.Begin and end it only with tenant.Commit (ST-SUP-RP04-LC03) or a rollback, and MUST NOT call Commit on the store transaction itself; the store pool that they take MUST be one that tenant.Open returned, so a connection that comes back with a tenant set is closed. The command runtime MUST check that pool with tenant.Opened when it is constructed (ST-SUP-RP04-LC08). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: Run decides the command's permission on its resource before the fill
statement: Run MUST decide the command's declared permission on the resource that the request names, after the bind and before the idempotency wrapper, through the authorization handle at the revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09), with the same consistency whether or not the row exists, after it reads the resource row through the bound transaction FOR SHARE, also for the parent of a create, never FOR KEY SHARE, which does not block the revocation's UPDATE of the token,, so no revocation can change its token before the command ends; a deny and a missing row MUST return ErrDenied, which the handler answers with 404, the same as a read (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06), and MUST NOT call the fill or write a key row. This answers ST-SUP-Q60 with option A. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); the share lock and the one consistency come from the review of PR #178. FOR SHARE only, and the token statement as one SELECT with no subselect and no comment that counts, come from the re-review of PR #178 at d773ffde. The token statement MUST match as a whole the form SELECT <column> FROM <table> WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND <key> = $2[::<type>] FOR SHARE, with plain identifiers, and hold no quote, dollar quote, comment, parenthesis, WITH, TABLE or VALUES. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); final check of PR #178 at 437d9c18. A create of an entity with no parent names no row, so Run MUST decide its permission on the service-level resource <resource type>:<service name>, such as service:todo-svc, as Provision does (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09), with no row to read; the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that a write to a missing or a denied row is answered 404, the same as a read (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06): one rule for every operation.

title: Slot code makes a loaded value from a validated request
statement: The runtime MUST give generated slot code a function that makes the loaded value of an entity from the request entity after the request is validated, and MUST NOT give a fill any way to make one, so the probe of a slot binding reads its entity fields from a value the fill did not build. This answers ST-SUP-Q63. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: The command runtime serves a command over HTTP and gRPC
statement: The command runtime MUST give Serve, an HTTP serving helper, and ServeRPC, a gRPC serving helper, that bind the verified tenant and principal, read the idempotency key, decode the request, call Run, map ErrDenied to 404, a declared refusal to its declared status and code, ErrConflict to 409 conflict and ErrCommitUnknown and any other error to 500 internal, and write the outcome audit row and the problem body; and it MUST give the contract helpers that never change, the type Refusal, NewID, ValidUUID and the entity and pointer helpers, so that the code that is the same for every command is not emitted and generated code passes only the spec of each command (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: The command runtime exports the bind, the outcome map and the outcome row of a request
statement: The command runtime MUST export BindIdentity, which takes the tenant from the verified claim and maps the verified identity to its principal of the declared subject type and refuses a context with no verified identity or no tenant claim; OutcomeOf, which maps an error of Run to its status, its fixed code and its audit outcome as Serve answers them (ST-SUP-RP10-LC33), with a declared refusal known by its value; and RecordFailure, which writes the outcome audit row of a request whose Run failed in its own short transaction that the end of the request does not cancel and gives the fixed code to the completion log; and Serve and ServeRPC MUST use these same functions, so a handler that decodes its own body, such as a handler of generated CRUD, emits none of these steps (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). No error text MUST reach the answer, the audit row or the log. The owner delegated the decision to the orchestrator, who decided option (a) of ST-SUP-Q96 on 2026-11-11.

title: The query handle is bound to one read-only transaction, tenant and principal
statement: Handle MUST be constructed only with the open read-only store transaction, the tenant and the principal that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose the tenant and the principal for reading only, with no way to change any of the three. The query handle MUST be bound only to a transaction at READ COMMITTED, which binding checks with current_setting('transaction_isolation'), so the revocation floor is read fresh for each statement (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09) whatever the role's default isolation is. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: No raw database connection is reachable through the query handle
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose a *sql.DB, *sql.Tx, *sql.Conn, a driver connection or a method that takes SQL text, and MUST reach storage only through the generated, tenant-scoped repository reads of the entities the query declares it reads.

title: Every read runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set
statement: Each repository read the handle offers MUST run in the bound transaction, with the transaction-local tenant set and the tenant predicate added, so a fill cannot read a row of another tenant.

title: The query handle can write nothing
statement: The handle MUST offer no create, update, delete, relate, unrelate or effect staging, and the bound transaction MUST be READ ONLY, so a write that reaches the database through any path still fails there.

title: The query handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor
statement: The handle's authorization part MUST be the authorization runtime's handle bound to the same transaction, tenant and principal, so each decision runs with the principal as subject at the consistency floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 states, and MUST offer no other decision path, no bypass and no relate or unrelate.

title: A read of a protected resource needs an allow
statement: Each read the handle makes of an entity with a resource type MUST first evaluate the permission that the entity declares for read through the authorization handle, and MUST return a deny as not found with no data from the row. A read MUST evaluate that permission also when no row exists, with a zero row token, so a missing row and a denied row cost the same calls; it MUST decide on the stored key of the row, not the caller's form of it; and a provider failure MUST give the same error whether or not the row exists. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A list through the query handle holds only allowed rows
statement: A list the handle returns for an entity with a resource type MUST be filtered by the decision port, on the query's declared permission for a list query and on the permission the entity declares for list otherwise, in the way the entity's expected cardinality declares, and every page MUST be checked at the one at_least floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC04 and ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 give a list. One list call MUST scan at most a fixed number of rows of the table, 1,000, in chunks of at least 100, and MUST return More with a cursor at the last key it scanned also when the page holds fewer items than its limit, so a principal with little access never makes one call scan the whole table. The first page MUST use no cursor predicate, so a key of any type works. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A read of personal data is audited per resource with the action read
statement: When the fill reads a resource of an entity with a pii field, Run MUST record one audit row for each such resource with the action read, the principal as the actor and the query name as operation (ST-SUP-RP05-LC01), each in its own short transaction as ST-SUP-RP05-LC02 states, through the audit connections of ST-SUP-RP10-LC29, before the result returns, and MUST return no result when a write fails. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: The query handle is invalid once the fill returns
statement: As soon as the fill returns or panics, before Run ends the transaction, every method of the handle and of its authorization part MUST return an error and read nothing, so a fill that keeps the handle, or a goroutine it started, cannot read outside its query.

title: A failed or panicking fill returns no result
statement: When the fill returns an error or panics, Run MUST end the transaction, make the handle invalid and return no result, with an error that does not carry the panic value. A fill that does not return normally, also through runtime.Goexit, MUST be treated as a panic: Run MUST return no result, make the handle and its probe invalid and roll the transaction back. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: The handle gives the fill its query's probe
statement: Handle MUST give the fill, through Probe, the typed probe that the generated code built for its query and bound to the handle's span context, tenant, principal and query name (ST-SUP-RC34-OC03), and MUST offer no other probe, writer or logger; as ST-SUP-RP11-LC09 states for the rest of the handle, that probe MUST emit nothing once the fill returns or panics (ST-SUP-RP12-LC02).

title: Each entity value through the query handle is a loaded value
statement: Each read operation of the handle MUST return the entity as its generated loaded type, such as LoadedReservation, which carries the stored field values and has no exported constructor, no exported field and no conversion from another type, so a fill can get a loaded value only from the handle and cannot build one itself. Its Value MUST return a deep copy of the stored field values, so a change to a slice or a map that the fill got never changes what the handle later sends, writes or decides on. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A streamed query sends only allowed loaded values, each decided at the floor
statement: For a query served as a server stream, the handle MUST offer Send, which MUST take only a loaded entity value (ST-SUP-RP11-LC12), MUST decide the read permission that the entity declares for it with the principal as subject at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 at the time of the send, MUST send the message only on an allow and drop and count it on a deny, MUST read through the bound read-only transaction alone, and MUST return an error and send nothing once the stream ends or the fill returns.

title: The query runtime commits and opens its pool only through the tenant runtime
statement: Run MUST open each read-only transaction with tenant.Begin and end it only with tenant.Commit (ST-SUP-RP04-LC03) or a rollback, and MUST NOT call Commit on the store transaction itself; the store pool that it takes MUST be one that tenant.Open returned. The query runtime MUST check that pool with tenant.Opened when it is constructed (ST-SUP-RP04-LC08). The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A cursor has an opaque text form bound to its query
statement: A query cursor MUST have a text form for the next HTTP request that is opaque to the client: its position MUST be sealed with an AEAD under a key derived from the service's cursor key, with the service, the query name, the tenant and the principal as associated data, so the text shows no key, provider cursor or token, and the cursor MUST be refused, with no rows read, when it was changed or is used for another service, query, tenant or principal. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); the AEAD comes from the review of PR #178.

title: A read audit row carries the outcome's error code
statement: A read audit row MUST carry the error_code of a read that failed, as a fixed code with no error text, and none for a read that succeeded. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: The query runtime serves a query over HTTP
statement: The query runtime MUST give an HTTP serving helper, Serve, that binds the verified identity to the tenant, the principal and the probe call, decodes the request, runs the query, writes the response and maps refusals to problem responses; a list helper that reads the limit parameter and writes the page body; the type Refusal; a refusal lookup in query.HTTP, Refusal func(error) (status int, code string, ok bool), which the generated code sets to queries.Declared, so that Serve answers a refusal that the lookup knows with its status and code, and writes the code in the problem response and the completion log, not in the read audit row, which the query runtime writes when the fill reads the row (ST-SUP-RP11-LC08); and the row reads Row.Int32, Row.Float, Row.Bytes and Row.JSON; so the code that is the same for every service is not emitted (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05), and generated code passes only what varies with the declaration. The owner delegated the serving helper to the orchestrator (2026-11-09); the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the bind, the list helper, the refusal type and the row reads move into the runtime as well, and that query.HTTP takes the refusal lookup. The orchestrator decided under the owner's delegation (2026-11-11, ST-SUP-Q95, option a) that the refusal code goes to the problem response and the completion log only.

title: A list orders by declared fields with the key last
statement: Repository.List MUST order by the declared fields that the query gives, each ascending or descending, with the key as the last tie-breaker, and the sealed cursor of ST-SUP-RP11-LC15 MUST hold the position of each order field and of the key, so that the next page starts after the last row of the page in that order with no row twice and no row left out; it MUST refuse an order field that the entity does not declare, and MUST give no total count. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: The query runtime serves a query over gRPC
statement: The query runtime MUST give a unary gRPC serving helper, ServeRPC, and a server stream helper, ServeStream, that take from the generated code only what varies with the declaration and with the method's messages (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). ServeRPC MUST run the steps of Serve (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17) with the request message in place of the HTTP request: bind the verified identity of the call's context, read the text of a list cursor from the request message with ParseCursor before any transaction, decode the request, run the query with Run and the fill, Next and Encode of the query's HTTP handler, and read the JSON body that Encode writes into a new response message with protojson, which drops a member that the message does not declare. ServeStream MUST bind the verified identity, decode the request, run the query's Stream function on RunStream (ST-SUP-RP11-LC13) once, and send each allowed value as its JSON form read into a new stream message; a send that the transport refuses MUST end the stream with the transport's status. Both MUST answer a failed bind Unauthenticated, a bad cursor or request InvalidArgument, a row that is not there or is denied NotFound, a read that could not be decided Unavailable, a declared refusal with the gRPC code of its HTTP status and its fixed code as the message, and every other error Internal with the code internal; the message of each status MUST hold no error text and no data of a row, the completion log MUST get the fixed code, and the count of the values that a deny dropped MUST NOT reach the client. BindRPC MUST take the request ID of the audit rows from the x-request-id request metadata. The orchestrator's brief of 2026-11-11 gives the gRPC methods of the runtime data path (ST-SUP-RC07-OC19, ST-SUP-RC33-OC08) to the query runtime, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC33 gives them to the command runtime.

title: A probe takes no free-text message
statement: The runtime's emit function MUST take only a generated observation descriptor and typed values that match the descriptor's fields in order, and MUST offer no message, format string, free attribute, error value or other parameter that the declaration does not declare; an emission with a value of the wrong kind or count, or with a measure outside its declared range, MUST be dropped and counted, never sent.

title: A probe is bound to its call and goes quiet once the fill returns
statement: A probe MUST be constructed only with the span context, the tenant, the principal and the name of the command, query, worker or slot binding that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose no way to change any of them; as soon as the fill returns or panics, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC09 state for the handle, each method of the probe MUST emit nothing and count the attempt, so a fill that keeps the probe, or a goroutine it started, cannot emit outside its call.

title: A log record carries opaque correlation only
statement: Each log record and console line MUST carry the name, the trace ID and span ID of the bound span context when it is valid, the tenant ID, the principal's opaque ID and the operation name, which the runtime adds and the fill cannot set, and MUST NOT carry a name, an email address or a claim of the principal; who did what stays in the audit trail (ST-SUP-RP05).

title: An event becomes a log record and a span event
statement: When the telemetry runtime (ST-SUP-RP03) has a log provider, each emission of an event MUST become one log record named domain.<name> with the declared severity, the declared fields as attributes and no body text, and, when the bound span is recording, one event of the same name on that span with only the attributes that ST-SUP-RP12-LC13 allows.

title: A counter or histogram becomes a metric
statement: When the telemetry runtime has a meter provider, each counter MUST be one monotonic integer counter named domain.<name> that adds one for each emission, and each histogram one floating-point histogram named domain.<name> in its declared unit that records the emitted value, each with only the attributes that ST-SUP-RP12-LC13 allows.

title: OTLP is on when a collector endpoint is set
statement: The runtime MUST send OTLP signals through the telemetry runtime when, and only when, the telemetry runtime has a collector endpoint at start.

title: The console sink writes one line per emission to standard output
statement: When ST-SUP-RP12-LC16 turns it on for declared observations, the console sink MUST write one line for each of their emissions of every kind to the process's standard output, as one JSON object or one logfmt line, with the timestamp, the severity, the service name, the instance identity, the name, the declared fields, the histogram value, the stego.outcome of an observation that counts each attempt, and the correlation of ST-SUP-RP12-LC03.

title: Emitting never blocks, fails or panics the fill
statement: An emission MUST return with no result and MUST NOT wait on a sink: each sink MUST take records through its own bounded queue of at most 1,024 records that drops rather than blocks, and a failing or blocked sink MUST NOT change, delay or stop the call.

title: A probe carries no private value
statement: The runtime MUST send only the declared fields, the histogram value and the correlation of ST-SUP-RP12-LC03, MUST cut each text value to at most 256 bytes of valid UTF-8, and MUST NOT add a request path, a query value, a body, a header, a credential, error text or a stack. It MUST NOT read a value from the context other than the bound span context.

title: The recorder captures every emission in order
statement: Recorder MUST be a sink that keeps every emission in memory in the order of the calls, with its name, kind, severity, fields, value, stego.outcome and correlation, MUST never drop one and MUST be safe for concurrent use. A probe bound to a recorder MUST send to no other sink. A probe that a generated test constructor binds MUST hold its emissions as ST-SUP-RP12-LC20 states until the test ends the call with a commit or a rollback, so a fill test can assert a rolled_back attempt and the absence of committed work.

title: A fill test asserts an emission by name and fields
statement: Recorder MUST offer the emissions of one observation, a check that fails the test when no emission of an observation has the given field values, and a check that fails the test when an observation was emitted at all; each failure MUST name the observation and list what was recorded.

title: Shutdown drains the console queue inside the shared budget
statement: Close MUST write the records queued for the console sink inside the one shared shutdown limit of ST-SUP-RC17-OC29 and ST-SUP-RP03-LC10, with no budget of its own, also when standard output blocks, and an emission after Close MUST be dropped and counted.

title: A span event and a metric carry no tenant or principal
statement: A span event MUST carry only the declared fields of its observation and its stego.outcome, and a metric only the declared fields, its stego.outcome and the operation name; neither MUST carry a tenant, a principal, a trace ID or a span ID, in line with ST-SUP-RP03-LC06, ST-SUP-RP03-LC11, ST-SUP-RP03-LC13 and ST-SUP-RC17-OC01.

title: The probe uses the telemetry runtime's providers only
statement: The probe MUST send OTLP signals only through the providers of the telemetry runtime, and MUST NOT create a provider, an exporter or a connection of its own.

title: A domain histogram has fixed boundaries and cumulative temporality
statement: Each domain histogram MUST use the fixed bucket boundaries of its unit, which are those of ST-SUP-RP03-LC11 for s; 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1,000, 2,500, 5,000 and 10,000 for ms; the powers of four from 64 to 67,108,864 for By; and 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1,000 for 1, and MUST use cumulative temporality, as ST-SUP-RP03-LC11 states for the request metrics.

title: Domain observations reach the console only when the environment turns it on
statement: The console sink MUST write the emissions of declared observations only when STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE is json or logfmt at start, and MUST NOT write them when the setting is absent or off, also when no collector endpoint is set; any other value MUST fail the start with fixed error text that does not echo the value.

title: No fill or declaration chooses a sink
statement: The probe, the fill and the declaration MUST NOT be able to choose a sink, a writer or a format: only the process environment at start chooses them.

title: The console sink opens no connection
statement: The console sink MUST start no OpenTelemetry provider and open no connection, so ST-SUP-RP03-LC01 holds without a collector.

title: Drops and write failures are counted
statement: The runtime MUST count the dropped records and the write failures of each sink, and MUST export the counts as the counters domain.probe.dropped and domain.probe.failed, labelled by sink only, when a meter provider exists.

title: Emissions are sent as their observation counts
statement: The runtime MUST hold the emissions of one call, at most 64, until the generated code ends the call's transaction, where a query that ends without an error counts as a commit, a slot binding's call ends with the transaction of the handler that calls it, and each attempt of a command that Run runs again after a conflict (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) is a call of its own. It MUST then send each emission of an observation that counts each attempt with the attribute stego.outcome set to committed or rolled_back, MUST send each emission of an observation that counts committed work only at a commit, without that attribute, and MUST drop it at a rollback. An emission beyond 64 MUST be dropped and counted.

title: Built-in service events go through the probe
statement: The runtime MUST offer the fixed service events of the telemetry runtime (telemetry.runtime.started, telemetry.runtime.stopped, service.ready, service.stopping, service.failed and http.server.diagnostic), the worker event worker.run.failed and the worker counters worker.tick.skipped and worker.tenant.unreached as built-in observations with their own fixed names and severities, with no fields except the worker name of each worker observation and the fixed outcome of worker.run.failed (ST-SUP-RC35-OC09), and never a tenant, so each worker counter has at most one series for each declared worker and at most 127 in all (ST-DECL-INV79, ST-SUP-RC17-OC17), sent to OTLP when a collector endpoint is set and to the console sink as ST-SUP-RP12-LC22 states, and a declared observation MUST NOT take one of their names.

title: Built-in service events are always on the console
statement: The console sink MUST always write each built-in service event (ST-SUP-RP12-LC21) to standard output as one JSON line in its fixed form, with the timestamp, the severity, the service name, the instance identity, the event name, and the trace ID and span ID when they are valid, with or without a collector endpoint and whatever STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE says, also off; such a line carries no tenant, principal or entity value.

title: Schema backfill observations are built in
statement: The runtime MUST offer the built-in counters schema.backfill.rows, schema.backfill.failed_rows and schema.backfill.duplicate_groups and the built-in events schema.backfill.completed (info) and schema.backfill.stalled (error), each with the one field change, an enum of the IDs of the declaration's open schema changes, at most 127 (ST-DECL-INV64), sent to the sinks as a declared observation is, and a declared observation MUST NOT take one of their names.

title: The verified identity is the only Identity, and it is sealed
statement: Verify MUST be the only way to make an Identity value. The Identity MUST hold the verified tenant claim inside the IdentityMark of the module's internal seal package, made by its internal constructor, so tenant.Claim (ST-SUP-RP04-LC01) reads the tenant from the mark through seal.TenantOf and never from a method that an outer type can declare again, and no package outside the runtime module can make one. The Identity MUST hold the verified issuer, the verified subject as the user ID, the roles, the tenant claim and the profile claims of ST-SUP-RP13-LC18, each read only after every check passes, and MUST offer no setter.

title: No claim is given before every check passes
statement: Verify MUST NOT give a claim to its caller before the signature, the issuer, the audience, the subject, the issue time and the expiry all pass, and MUST return no partial identity with an error.

title: The declared algorithms of the allow list RS256 and ES256 only, each with its own key type
statement: Verify MUST accept only the algorithms that the settings name from its fixed allow list, which is RS256 and ES256, and RS256 alone when the settings name none; New MUST refuse settings that name any other algorithm or one algorithm twice; Verify MUST refuse alg none, every HMAC algorithm and every other algorithm whatever the key says, MUST refuse a token whose algorithm is not the one algorithm of the key that its key ID selects (RS256 for an RSA key, ES256 for a P-256 key), and MUST refuse a token with a typ other than JWT or with a crit, jku, jwk or x5u header. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider (ST-SUP-RC37); where the oidc-auth contracts are silent on a security choice, the builder took the strict one.

title: The RSA key size is bounded
statement: The key set MUST refuse an RSA public key with fewer than 2048 bits, more than 8192 bits, or an exponent other than 65537.

title: Trust settings are explicit at construction
statement: New MUST refuse settings whose issuer is not an HTTPS URL, whose audience is empty, or whose clock skew is negative or more than 60 seconds, and Verify MUST check the issuer and the audience by exact match, MUST refuse an aud that is neither a string nor an array whose every member is a string, and MUST check the expiry and the issue time against the clock with that skew, refusing a token at exactly its exp as RFC 7519 states.

title: Oversize, ambiguous and invalid tokens are refused
statement: Verify MUST refuse a raw token that holds any character other than the base64url alphabet and the two dots, a token larger than 16 KiB, a header or payload with a duplicate member or more than 32 levels of nesting, and a payload with an unpaired Unicode surrogate escape.

title: One exact key ID, no fallback, and bounded key documents
statement: The key set MUST select only the key whose key ID matches the token's exactly and MUST NOT fall back to another key; MUST read the members of the key document by their exact names, with no folding of case; and MUST refuse a key document larger than 64 KiB, with a repeated key ID or with more than 32 keys.

title: The remote key source uses verified TLS with no redirect and no proxy
statement: The remote key source MUST load the key document, and the discovery document of an issuer source (ST-SUP-RP13-LC21), only from an HTTPS URL over verified TLS 1.2 or later, MUST NOT follow a redirect and MUST NOT send the request through an HTTP proxy; a configured CA file MUST add its certificates to the system roots and MUST NOT replace them.

title: An unknown key ID refreshes the cache under a rate limit
statement: The key set MUST answer a known key ID from its cache with no request; when the cache is older than its refresh age, it MUST answer a known key ID from the cache at once, within the outage window of ST-SUP-RP13-LC10, while one refresh runs; it MUST refresh the key document once when a token names an unknown key ID, and only that token MUST wait for the refresh, with one request for each refresh and at least 30 seconds between attempts; and it MUST deny the token when the refresh is in its cooldown or the key ID is still unknown after it.

title: A bounded outage window, and a removed key stops at once
statement: The key set MUST deny every token 15 minutes after the last successful key load until a later load succeeds, and MUST deny at once a token whose key the replacement key document does not hold.

title: Stop closes the verifier, and a zero value fails closed
statement: After Stop, Verify MUST deny every token and a repeat Stop MUST be safe; Stop MUST cancel a key retrieval that is running and deny the request that started it; and a zero value of the verifier or the key set MUST deny every token.

title: Errors and telemetry hold no token, claim or provider detail
statement: An error or a telemetry record of the package MUST NOT contain the token, a claim value, a key ID, a key document, the source URL, a file path or the provider's response text, and a cache hit, a cooldown refusal or a stopped verifier MUST emit no refresh telemetry.

title: Claims map to the principal, the roles and the tenant from configured paths only
statement: Verify MUST read the subject only from the configured subject claim, a top-level claim that is sub when none is configured, and New MUST refuse a subject claim that is a path or a registered claim other than sub (iss, aud, exp, nbf, iat, jti); verify MUST read the roles only from the configured role claim path and the tenant only from the configured tenant claim path, with no fallback to another claim, as ST-SUP-RC11-OC08 states; a role path that is configured but absent from the token MUST give no roles; a role claim that is present but is not an array of at most 128 clean strings of at most 256 bytes MUST be refused; a tenant claim that is not one clean string of 1 to 255 bytes MUST be refused; and Verify MUST make the principal from the verified issuer and subject pair.

title: The bearer middleware takes exactly one credential and denies safely
statement: Middleware MUST refuse a request whose configured header does not hold exactly one Bearer credential, also on a custom header, unless the declaration opts that header in to a bare token, for a proxy such as oauth2-proxy that forwards the token alone; MUST put the verified Identity in the request context only after Verify passes; and MUST answer a refusal with 401, Cache-Control no-store, a WWW-Authenticate header and the problem body of ST-SUP-RP13-LC17, with no token in the response.

title: The verifier is safe for concurrent use
statement: Verify MUST give the same verified identity to concurrent callers of the same token, and the key set MUST make at most one refresh request at a time.

title: authntest serves a local key document and mints test tokens
statement: The package authntest MUST serve a key document over TLS on 127.0.0.1 with a test certificate authority that it makes, MUST mint tokens with the claims, the key and the header a test gives, including invalid ones, and MUST be imported by no file other than a test file; its key server MUST stop when the test ends.

title: The 401 body is the service's problem document
statement: A refusal of the middleware MUST answer with the problem body of ST-SUP-RC20-OC01, OC03 and OC04: the content type application/problem+json, the type made of the declared error type base and unauthorized, or about:blank when none is declared, the title, the status 401, the code made of the declared service prefix and AUT-001, a fixed detail, the request path as instance and the time as timestamp; the settings MUST carry the problem type and the problem code from the declaration, and the body MUST hold no token, claim or key data.

title: The Identity carries the profile claims
statement: The Identity MUST carry, after every check passes, the claims that the jwt-auth verifier gives today (ST-SUP-RC11-OC08): the roles, the configured attributes, preferred_username, email, given_name and family_name, each a clean string of at most 256 bytes when present and empty when absent, and a present claim of the wrong type MUST be refused.

title: A PEM public key file is a key source, for tokens with no key ID
statement: The key set MUST accept, as its source instead of a key document, a PEM file that holds one RSA public key within the bounds of ST-SUP-RP13-LC04; with that source, Verify MUST accept a token with no kid and MUST refuse a token that names a kid, and the key MUST be read once at start, with a load failure refusing the start.

title: Authenticate verifies a credential for the shared-context transports
statement: The package MUST offer Authenticate, which takes the context and the raw credential that a transport other than HTTP read, such as a gRPC metadata value, applies the credential rules of ST-SUP-RP13-LC14 and Verify, and returns a context that holds the Identity, so every transport reaches the same checks.

title: An issuer is found through its discovery document, read once at start
statement: A key set whose source is an issuer MUST load the discovery document <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration once at start under the rules of the remote key source (ST-SUP-RP13-LC08), with the bounds and the JSON rules of a key document (ST-SUP-RP13-LC06, LC07); MUST refuse the start when the document cannot be loaded, when its issuer member is not exactly the issuer, or when its jwks_uri member is not an HTTPS URL; MUST then load the key document from that jwks_uri as from a key URL (ST-SUP-RP13-LC07 to LC10); and MUST NOT load the discovery document again while it runs, so a refresh reads only the key document. The source MUST refuse an issuer that is not an HTTPS URL or that holds a query. Each refusal MUST name the discovery document and MUST hold no URL or provider text (ST-SUP-RP13-LC12). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider (ST-SUP-RC37); where the oidc-auth contracts are silent on a security choice, the builder took the strict one.

title: An ES256 key is a P-256 point, and its signature is r and s
statement: The key set MUST read a key of kty EC and crv P-256 as an ES256 key when its alg is ES256 or absent, MUST refuse a key document that holds such a key whose x or y is not exactly 32 bytes of base64url or whose point is not on the curve, and MUST skip an EC key of another curve or with another alg; Verify MUST check an ES256 signature as the 64 bytes of r and s that RFC 7518 section 3.4 states, and MUST refuse a signature of another length or form. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider (ST-SUP-RC37); where the oidc-auth contracts are silent on a security choice, the builder took the strict one.

title: Settings come from the process environment by fixed names
statement: Settings MUST be read from the process environment by fixed names, DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL or STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_AUTHN_ISSUER, STEGO_AUTHN_AUDIENCE, STEGO_AUTHN_KEYS_URL or STEGO_AUTHN_KEYS_FILE, STEGO_AUTHN_CA_FILE, STEGO_SPICEDB_ENDPOINT, STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE, STEGO_SPICEDB_INSECURE_LOOPBACK, STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE and STEGO_SERVICE_VERSION, with the settings of the auth provider that the declaration states for the verifier (jwt-auth, or oidc-auth with discovery through its issuer, where no key document setting may be set), and MUST refuse a missing or malformed setting with an error that names the setting and not its value. A file that a setting names, DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE and STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE, MUST be read only when it is at an absolute path, is a regular file of at most 64 KiB, opens without a wait on a FIFO, has no execute bit and is not writable by group or other; else the setting MUST be refused. The orchestrator decided the key files under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), from finding 5 of the security baseline review of the runtime. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: New wires the runtimes of a service from its settings
statement: New MUST take the Settings and the declared parts, open the two pools through tenant.Open with the connection configuration of the adapter, connect to SpiceDB with the preshared key, start the telemetry and the probes, and give the verifier, the authorization runtime, the audit writer, the outbox queue and the command and query runtimes, so that the code that is the same for every service is not emitted and generated code passes only what varies with the declaration (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: Migrate runs the migration job in one fixed order
statement: Migrate MUST take the ordered migration texts and the schema writer and run the migration job on one connection, with a time limit, in this order: the read-only ledger check, WriteSchema, the ledger of the adapter with the tenant list of the tenant runtime (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07), the outbox, audit, idempotency and authorization migrations, the grants of the runtime role, the audit partitions and WriteSchema; and it MUST stop at the first step that fails, with a fault that names the step. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11. The orchestrator decided ST-SUP-Q97 (a) on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation: the tables step makes the tenant list.

title: Start runs the workers of the selected modes, and Shutdown stops them once
statement: Start MUST start, for the modes that the process runs (ST-SUP-RP09-LC01), the components that the records give each mode and no other: in the worker mode the outbox worker with the destinations of the service's components, the authorization relay as its destination authz and the relay's late-revocation watch (ST-SUP-RC18-OC25, ST-SUP-RP06-LC06, ST-SUP-RP06-LC14), on a pool of the worker role and a pool of the relay login role, each opened through tenant.Open from the fixed settings STEGO_WORKER_DATABASE_URL and STEGO_RELAY_DATABASE_URL or their file forms; in the controller mode the audit anchor job at the declared anchor period and the audit maintenance loop as periodic jobs under the controller lease stego.controller, so two replicas never run the same job (ST-SUP-RP09-LC13, ST-SUP-RC28-OC08); and in the api mode no component. The migration job MUST make the lease table and the row of the controller lease in its audit step, with SELECT and UPDATE for the runtime role. The readiness MUST answer each selected mode (ST-SUP-RP09-LC05) and name each component that stopped and each job that is not healthy, and no tenant. Shutdown MUST make every mode not ready, run the shutdown of each selected mode in its own order (ST-SUP-RP09-LC06), release the controller lease, end every component and close the worker and relay pools, once for each process whatever the number of calls. A selection that runs the worker mode without the worker role's connection string MUST be refused, naming the setting and not its value. The owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the runtime data path is the only data path; the orchestrator's brief of that date gives the worker process to the service runtime.

title: A declared issuer gives the verifier its discovered key set, and a refused start names its stage
statement: New MUST make the key set of a declaration that states discovery from the issuer (ST-SUP-RP13-LC21) with the CA file, and the verifier with the declared algorithms and subject claim; and StartStage MUST give the stage service.start.authn.discovery for a start that a discovery document refused, service.start.authn.keys for a start that another key source refused, and no stage for every other failure, so the failure record of the process names the cause with no error text. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider (ST-SUP-RC37); where the oidc-auth contracts are silent on a security choice, the builder took the strict one.
